title: Agreements in Distant Malaysia
desc:
Since the small circle of people close to Pahan had full access to the outside world, not counting the majority of the country's isolated civilian population, interesting information was obtained from Asia. The recently formed Malaysian state, which rose from under Japanese influence and gained independence as a result of a brutal war, is gradually opening up to the world. Some American diplomatic channels have been reporting for the past two months on the Malaysian government's willingness to cede some control over its natural resources to investors in exchange for assistance in industrialization.

The Americans were, of course, the first to respond, taking indirect control of the resource-rich capital city of Kuala Lumpur. We, of course, do not have as many resources as the leading OFN state, but we do have something to offer in exchange. In exchange for our equipment and several large civilian enterprises located in Tyumen, we will gain a valuable trading partner, while receiving the rubber that Russia so desperately needs. We need it for the production of combat aircraft, but on paper and in official documentation, this rubber will be used exclusively for civilian purposes. Who knows, maybe this work will turn into something more in the future?

title: A Noisy Night
desc:
A gang of bandits rushed to the hall. They were carrying expensive liquor, most of them already drunk after looting and drinking most of the alcohol they found in an old warehouse. 

 As they sat down they sat in a large dining hall, the realization of their achievement set in. They wondered how a conqueror would celebrate such an occasion. A feast! The old Nikolai shouted. He remembered hearing stories of old kings holding massive feast for important events. 

The men agreed, they wanted to feel like the tsars of old. 

Everything they could find would go for it. They slaughtered cattle, looted more liquor stores and graved the most expensive cigars they could find. 

They were going to dine like kings and nothing was going to take this joy from their hands.

title: Unforeseen Developments
desc:
Ioseliani stumbled out of the hangar where another victory feast was being held, doubling over and vomiting, the alcohol running through his veins expelling itself. The night was dark and silent, aside from the shouts and light coming out of the hangar door. 

The Great Pakhan tensed up at hearing the crunch of footsteps behind him, his hand quickly finding his pistol and looking over his shoulder. 

"Ah... Rafael..." 

Ioseliani's face was stony as he straightened out and looked around, checking for people listening in, and silently pushed the door closed, nodding to his underling, allowing him to speak. 

Rafael's eyes darted around.  

"Jaba, we have Usoyan's accountant under our control" 

Ioseliani's face lit up as he slurred. "Well lovely stuff! Just a little more and that Kurdish snake will show its head!" 

"Jaba, the pakhans are making moves." 

"Fuck, Raf, be specific, the feast's still go-" 

"Some are stealing weapons, some are deviating from patrolling routes, some are setting up bases where they aren't supposed to... and the single person it all goes back to is... Ûsoyan. I think this may be the beginning of something big..." 

Ioseliani looked off into the dark, the haze of alcohol quickly being replaced with cold determination. 

"Bo-?" 

"Raf, get my coat." 

"Wh-" 

"We've been waiting for this opportunity, Raf! That damn Kurd is gonna get his due. ALL OF THEM ARE GOING TO GET THEIR DUE!" The Great Pakhan's stride lost any of the drunk slowness as he walked away from the hangar. "Raf-"

title: Thinking About Tomorrow
desc:
Ioseliani looked at the coin he twirled between his fingers, flicking it on the table, it spinning with a small ring, before slamming it down and repeating the same motion, over and over as his thoughts drifted for the first time in the many years he had been pakhan, even before it gained a 'Great' and got a capital letter. 

The truths of the gulag were simple: get the loyal in power, get the strong under you, make sure your suck ups keep their heads down. 

It was easy to be pakhan if you had the strength for it, but being the Great Pakhan? 

He had thought for a band of aimless men with fists for weapons, now he had to command an army. When before he just needed to feed himself and his goons for a day or two, the files on his desk talked of tonnes of flour and rice that would go to women and children in the cities. When before a mistake could at worst lead to a couple of kicked-in heads, now a nation balanced on a razor. 

The Great Pakhan slammed the coin down again and looked at the surface, the face of Nicholas the II staring back, a rare keepsake that one of his thieves found in the ground in Vorkuta. Ioseliani blinked, for a small fraction of a second the face that displayed the rotten Tzar morphing into his own, smiling victoriously. The Great Pakhan looked at the coin again and smirked. 

Glory did not wait for him to get comfortable, it ran ahead, and his thieves and he layed catch-up. Past the Vorkuta guards, past the communists and the omskovite fanatics, past his competition, Ioseliani continued to chase that spark. 

Glory did not wait for anybody. 

Ioseliani stood up, flipping the coin and stuffing it into his jacket pocket.

options.name: So he will continue giving chase.

title: The Neutral Option
desc:
Ioseliani unfurled the map of Europe onto his desk.  Good maps were hard to find these days -- this was one of the only few they could get him that wasn't 30 years out of date, and the rather unfortunate state of much of it lying under the Nazi jackboot made things pretty hard for Jaba.  The Thieves demanded money and power for his loyalty, but with the Swastika flying from Amsterdam to Moscow, there weren't exactly a lot of options he had left. 

Earlier, he had considered opening relations with the United States.  CIA agents had already involved themselves in training his troops, no doubt in exchange for hefty amounts of money and other...less legal things that only the Thieves in Law could provide.  One problem.  The Americans were an ocean away, and other than the frozen Kara and Laptev seas, the Thief Territory was landlocked. 

That left him with one option.  The neutral nations of Europe.  The German Sphere might have been out of his hands, but there was still money to be found on the continent.  Brittany was a state not unlike his own, and for the right price, they'll trade with anyone.  Pulling out a marker, he circled the country before moving south.  Switzerland was another good option.  Neutral and rich.  Iberia and Italy were perhaps even more lucrative.  With empires of their own and mutual hate for the Germans, a lucrative relationship could be made, both with their governments, and with the Italian and Iberian Mafias.  The Great Pakhan smiled.  There was hope for Europe yet.

title: The Caudillo
desc:
Franco looked much more imposing in the propaganda photos, thought Ioseliani.  The old man standing in front of him, cane in hand, didn't seem like an imposing figure.  However, even though he didn't know a word of Spanish, he heard enough of the Caudillo's voice to know that he was not a man to be trifled with.  The Spanish, for such a laid-back people, sure loved their formalities.  He had been greeted with fine food, a Flamenco show, and a drill demonstration from the Iberian Army.  

When he at last sat down with the Caudillo to talk business, he was surprised that the two had a lot in common.  Both men had come to power in a time when their nation was gripped in weakness and civil war, a sentiment that resonated in Franco, that he was sure of from his firm handshake and that rare genuine smile he saw from the dictator.  The deal was simple.  Iberia would formally end its German-directed embargo on the free Russian territories and recognize the West Siberian Thief Territory as an independent state able to do business with Iberian corporations.  

Camera crews filmed and shutters flashed as the two dictators shook hands for all Iberia to see.  Two men that had risen from irrelevance to the very top.  Perhaps a lesser man would have come back with nothing, but Jaba knew a fellow self-made man when he saw one.  It was the cunning of this world, those that took risks and played hard, that would win.  And together, the Spanish Bull could make the Russian Bear roar again.

title: The Godfather
desc:
"I do not see how your... organization could even benefit us." Giuseppe let out a puff of smoke and stretched lazily. Ioseliani could understand the lack of sense of urgency in the mafioso's movements. In the end, the Great Pakhan had been effectively defanged to enter Cosa Nostra territory, no weapons, no associates, just him. They even took away the Imperial coin he kept for good luck. 

"Well, Mister-" 

"Padre." Giuseppe leaned forward, "You will call me... Padre." 

The Great Pakhan's lips reflexively thinned out, but he really had no choice. If he wanted to speak to the leader of the Sicilian Mafia, Giuseppe Genco Russo, he had to do it as a weaker associate, rather than a greater power. 

"Padre Giuseppe, I believe my nation has MANY benefits for your business." God, Ioseliani hated being sober, he never felt anxious, but the acute feeling that every word was being judged as a life-or-death matter did not leave him. 

"After all, behind me is a whole country. Huge markets, privileges with my security services, so much untouched land that you can hide your longer-term merchandise." 

"And what do you want then?" Giuseppe interrupted, his expression unreadable. 

"Well," Ioseliani grinned confidently, "Arms, support, eased trade and diplomacy with your group, as well as information on Italy-dearest's further interests and movements." 

Giuseppe's expression did not change, instead, it stayed static as the mafiosi considered. "Fine, this does interest me." Suddenly the Padre's tone warmed, "A drink to the new partnership?" 

The Great Pakhan chuckled, "Sure, always wanted to try Prosecco."

title: A True Tax Haven
desc:
Ioseliani felt out of place at this table, his neatly-pressed suit incomparable to the lavishness of the international tycoons, let alone their diamond-studded wives, all wearing the same painted-on smiles. 

One of the presenters fumbled a paper, beginning to announce the next orator for the evening, "Well, and to our newly accepted guest of honour! While the Swiss Alps may never compare to the Urals I would like to welcome Mister Jaba IO- IOSE- !?" 

The Great Pakhan gave a wry irritated smile as he stood up, champagne in his hand, the glass giving a whine under the pressure of his fingers. "Ladies and Gentlemen, I would like to give a short toast before this evening moves forward!" 

The whole room applauded politely, but the coldness behind their eyes could not betray that this was a test... 

"All of us here, we are self-built men. Men who were given no quarter, and took none ourselves. Some during the Great Depression," Several of the silver-haired monocles nodded, "Some during the trying times of the Great Patriotic- I mean, the Second World War," This time it was the turn of the men of Ioseliani's age to grumble in agreement. 

"And some even now, during the Reich's attempts to get a foothold on both of our doorsteps. Therefore we must celebrate this liberty, this great gift granted to us, to work and to be rewarded! Tonight, we take it easy, but we must also take it now!" Ioseliani raised his champagne glass, the tycoons raising theirs in unison.

title: Towards the Tip of France
desc:
If North Russia had frozen him with ice, Northern France pelted Vadim with sloshing rain and howling wind, but unlike Northern Russia, he had nought but a leather jacket to combat the elements, each of his limbs feeling like it was cast from numb marble. 

"Damn fucking..." He swore under his breath as the salt sprays hit Vadim in the face, another barge lazily pulling into the port of Saint Malo, the grey waves parting underneath it, several exhausted French sailors trudging into port under the torrential rain. Though, one seemed to stay back, sitting on one of the crates with a dreary expression. 

Vadim felt a sudden empathy, "Guard duty?" 

The French soldier lifted his head, "Hm?" 

Vadim pointed at the boxes of guns his boss left him on guard duty with and then at his rifle, "Guard duty?" 

The French's face lit up with understanding, "Ah, surentez?" 

"Yes yes, er... surandes..." Vadim nodded. 

The French chuckled, fishing around in his pocket and taking out a cigarette pack and offering it to the equally exhausted Russian. "Sigaretenn?" 

"Sure..." Vadim took the cigarette, lighting the Frenchman's and then his, before turning back towards the Yugran barge, observing the crates of guns with a bored expression. The French, turned back to his.

title: Approaching the Eagle
desc:
Ioseliani leaned back in the chair, eyeing the two agents sitting across him, as well as the huge mirror window on the wall. My, this certainly felt familiar. 

"So no press conferences and smiling at the camera?" The Great Pakhan pronounced dryly, picking between his teeth with a nail. 

Even through their shades, Ioseliani noted the glances the two agents threw at each other.  

"While the United States are open to negotiation in supporting your efforts, Mister Ioseliani-" 

"You cannot parade a 'criminal', hm?" Ioseliani interrupted. 

The agent opened his mouth, closed it, then opened it again. "Yes..." 

An unpleasant silence filled the room. Ioseliani chuckled. "Funny from a nation whose founding idea was tax evasion. But otherwise, what can you give me? Have you received the list I sent you?" 

Some of the tensions subsided as the other agent smiled. "We have looked through your demands and found none of them to be unreasonable. Actually, upon looking over your situation, we found that your resolve in allowing free markets and competition warrants additional support." 

A slip of paper with lines upon lines of equipment was slipped across the table, The Great Pakhan catching it and giving it a glance... 

Ioseliani stood up, before smiling, "So, we are doing this 'on the hush'?" 

The agents also stood up,

title: A Helping Hand
desc:
Agent Konrad sighed as he observed the thief militia that was put under his responsibility to be trained. While the CIA had arranged to send arms, they also got the bright idea to send actual military personnel to train these... thieves. 

Not a single one responded to names, many had utterly ignored him until their... 'pakhan'... had barked something in Russian, all of them suddenly straightened out and became at least partially workable. 

But this? This took the cake. Yesterday they were ordered to pick up their equipment, some unbranded military kits and now... 

"WHY?" Konrad rubbed his forehead while the pakhan relayed his message. 

Some of the soldiers stood with extra guns, while some held their night vision goggles like blunt weapons, clearly having exchanged them for extra pieces of whatever they wanted. 

There was the large unit that was Krokhin, also known by 'Alligator', who had exchanged his kit parts for MREs, slowly stuffing another packet of shredded beef down his gob, chewing lazily as he looked off into the distance with barely any attention. 

Then there was the anaemic 'Vova', his gear lacking in grenades but in surplus of three coats on his shoulders, staring back with an innocent look in his eyes. 

Konrad's eyes stopped on 'Pero' Pechurin and asked him directly. 

"WHY, PECHURIN!?" 

The thief smiled from under the monopolized mountain of helmets, his golden teeth reflecting amiably.

title: Assessing Our Potential
desc:
Batov marched in front of the row of soldiers, observing the new form of armed forces he would command. 

Some stood straight, he could recognize the deportment of his own officers, or of the forces of Kaganovich, some like the Omskovites didn't even seem to breathe. There was the more relaxed ones, Dragunov's boys. The last ones were of course the bandits, none having uniforms, many exchanging jokes as Batov passed them. 

The general turned on his heels, observing the line of mix-and-matched soldiers. "Krotov through Kalmikin, re-do basic training."  

The line of bandits went silent, shocked. "All the bandit forces are to re-do basic training, including discipline training and uniform rules." The General looked at the rest and shouted, "Toooooo the right!" 

The line turned ninety degrees, even the shocked bandits following orders. 

"Foooorward... MARCH!" The soldiers marched away towards the barracks, leaving Ioseliani, who up to now sat lazily on the sidelines, observing the General, and Batov alone on the field. 

Ioseliani broke the silence. "What the fuck was that? I thought we were working together you dust-bag!" 

Batov was not at all shifted by the change in tone. "The Territory's forces are not ready for combat, they lack discipline and they cannot follow orders efficiently, that is the base of the army." 

"Look, old boy," Ioseliani sat forward, it was clear he was barely containing his anger. "Each gang has a right to express their way in combat, you don't-" 

Batov chuckled. "Well, if they keep trying to undermine overall order, it won't matter how unique they are if they're dead in a ditch. When the sun goes down-"

title: What's in a Name
desc:
Pyotr scratched his beard with the dirt-covered rubber gloves, as always disappearing into his own thoughts as he tended to his field. 

But why the name, the Thieves? He could not really put a finger on it.  

Sure, their language was generally dirty, their attire was terrible and they carried guns wherever they went and used them with little to no control, but who didn't?  

Pyotr, in fact, saw LESS theft, not more than when Kaganovich was still the man with the crown. And working wasn't as unpleasant, after all, your own field feels much better than a community one, and who was he to start lying to himself? 

Yeah, they collected taxes, but at least they had the conscience to send some foul-mouthed gang pup to explain it first, rather than barging in and taking whatever they wanted.  

And the weekends? Pyotr had not had a weekend since... Well, he could not even remember when! Sure, he got longer breaks on Sundays, but otherwise, it was labour for 'The People' and 'The Party', day in and day out.  

And the sales! He'd never even bought or sold anything before! Sure, he bartered but knowing that you could trade for a day's food and some new book with the paper stacks you got from a tonne of potatoes somehow felt more reassuring than hoping that the Narkom was in good spirits on one day or another. 

Why, the fact he even thought about books was surprising! A couple of years back and he would just stare at those hieroglyph slips without a thought in the world! 

No, maybe they called themselves Thieves, Pyotr considered.

options.name: But he sure didn't see it..

title: The Long Road Home
desc:
Sergei Vorontzov pushed his cracked spectacles up his nose nervously, looking up at the entrance into what used to be... No, what is his land. The ten-hectare piece of land was good for a peasant farmer, in the better times... 

Sergei shook the apparition away with a shake of the head, before pushing the creaking gates open and walking in, the single bag on his back weighing on his weary shoulders covered in a dusty telogreika. 

His house was gone, so was his family, and while it was not something unexpected, he still felt a small painful pang in his heart. Instead, there was a single barn, a left-over of the collective that farmed the land. Wandering up to it, the old 'kulak' dropped his bag at the doorstep, turning around and sitting down on the dusty wooden stairs to observe his returned lands. 

Thirty years? Forty? His hand slowly found the small wooden cross on a rope and grasped it. Omsk, Sverdlovsk, Salechard, Vorkuta. They chased them further North then, farther from possible escape and warmer survivable weather. Farther from home. Farther from- 

The old man opened his mouth, clenching his teeth. "I'm home, Varvara... I'm home... I told you I would only be a while..."

options.name: A journey the length of a lifetime...

title: The Thief's World
desc:
Ioseliani tapped the pen on the paper, lifting his eyes at the mayor of the town. 

"Is that all?" 

The young man nodded, scratching his cheek, a prison tattoo on the top of his hand showing a smoking skull. 

"Certainly is. The people need some education, not enough engineers for the electrical substation. Also, the food reserves could get a re-fill, what with the collective farms being an utter fucking bust-" 

The Great Pakhan sighed, "Yeah yeah, stop yapping, I'm thinking." It certainly was a poignant problem, but the people were not only split by their identities, but by even how they got their daily piece of bread. 

Omskovites and Kaganovich's clique worked by what was essentially a command economy, Zlatoust stood on a sheer capitalist economy, though its social net was barely existent. Rokossovsky was a military junta and it worked completely by rationing, in the end, an army by itself was not very effective. 

But what was going to be THEIR economy? Ioseliani suddenly remembered the greatest mafiosis of his time. 

Al Capone, Siegel, Dillinger, all of them had tied the system around their finger, and which system was it? 

Ioseliani felt a grin spread on his lips. 

"I think we should privatize, I mean-"

title: An Unexpected Investment
desc:
Alexander stared at the two mooks sitting at his family table, his wife and children standing to the side, their looks teetering on mute terror.  

"Ah! The owner's here! Come on in!" The thinner bandit grinned and waved Alexander forward, to the table. While his exterior did seem friendly, the shopowner could not take his eyes off of the rifle on the bandit's knees. 

Alexander sat down and interlocked his fingers to control the shaking that entered his hands. "G-good evening. How may I help you?" 

"We have been hearing that your business is struggling, Mister Koroviev?" The taller bandit sat forward, observing the shopkeeper with a saccharine grin. 

"W-well..." Alexander was about to burst into hopeless tears, they were right, completely right. He did not have even enough money to get drivers for the goods trucks and had to drive them himself, but how could he tell that to the men who took gold and handed out lead at a moment's notice. 

The shopkeeper sighed, collecting all of his courage. Lying was pointless, and he wanted to make sure that whatever happens, he would not be remembered for cowardice. "Yes, I am struggling-" 

"Well, that's perfect! Congratulations, Mister Koroviev! Our local administration had heard these rumours and decided to help." 

Alexander was stunned, "P-pardon?" 

"You shall be receiving pay-outs starting next month to keep your business running. Though there is a condition." The taller bandit sat forward. 

Alexander nodded anxiously. "That being..?" 

The thin thief chuckled.

options.name: "We order you, you follow us! Simple as!"

title: Between a Rock And A Hard Place
desc:
The Great Pakhan put the cigarette out on the table, forcing an annoyed look from Batov. 

"Careful, these maps can go up in flames at a second's notice." The General's hand carefully pushed the huge rolls to the side, farther from the black spot on the surface. 

Ioseliani snorted and took a few more gulps from his bottle, "Enough with the semantics! What do we have?" 

Batov sighed, unfurling the map, "Two fronts, the West, and the East. Up to now, neither has agreed to diplomatic dialogue, yet, at least." 

"Mhm mhm." The Great Pakhan grumbled, scratching his chin. 

"In the West, we have the most industry of the past union. Big cities, huge factories, more infrastructure. Though fighting them will probably hurt like a bitch, considering that it was one of the most fractured regions, and it faced Finland off, they probably have much more experience." 

"And the East?" Ioseliani interrupted, his eyes thoughtful. 

Batov traced the Eastern frontier of their holdings. "Deeper into Siberia. Less infrastructure, but the whole region has benefited a great deal from the remains of Bukharin's so-called 'Siberian plan'. I do not know how much of it we can seize, but with the terrain and the lesser number of big cities can be challenging." The General stopped, looking over the Great Pakhan. 

"So? Where should we focus the forces?" 

Ioseliani snapped out of his thoughts, before yawning. 

"So the West's got most of the industry... that means most of the financial remains are there as well?" 

Batov blinked. "I... suppose?" 

Ioseliani smiled knowingly, "Then what are we waiting for?"

title: A State Against The State
desc:
Maria looked at her son entering the apartment, instantly noticing the scuffed uniform. 

"Vanechka, what happened, hm?"  

The young boy looked down at his shoes, before muttering, "A fight..." 

Maria shook her head and sighed, "Come, sit down." The boy would drop his school bag, and sit down at the dinner table, still not looking up from his knees. 

The young woman would sit down across him, "You know you can't keep going like this, right? Vanechka?" The boy would not respond. "Every week you come back like this, all dirty and beat, you HAVE to start growing up, son. You cannot solve your problems with your fists-" 

"It's all Zhenka's fault!" The boy would shout, raising his eyes, clearly about to burst into angry tears. "We promised that we wouldn't give each other out! Just because I stole some chalk, he gave me out like a dirty rat!" 

Maria sighed, keeping her voice as even as possible, "Vania, that is still not-" 

"Then why's Dad allowed to, and I'm not! I heard vors are supposed to look out for each other!" 

The young woman barely contained the surprise, "W-well..." 

The boy would sob and run out of the room, knocking over the chair, slamming the door behind him. 

"Vania!" Maria would try to follow but then sat back down, sighing again and rubbing her forehead. 

She did not know why her husband, a supposed vor v zakone, one who was never supposed to work with the government, suddenly became the Chief of local Police, or how he permitted himself to marry even though vors supposedly never married. She could not wrap her head around it either, just as her son.  

"'Vors', 'promises', 'honour'..."

options.name: "God, they're no more mature than Vania..."

title: The Power Struggle
desc:
The cracks are forming, the divisions have begun. 

Jaba Ioselani, the Great Pakhan, the visionary, the man of the people, the military man. His men are in the top rungs, his officers are in the military, their names are on plaques and official lists. The crown rests on his head as his tendrils sneak through the land, tying everything back to him. The Georgian Wolf, his fangs grasping region to region, trying to hold his allies together with a sure but loose grip. Idealists love him, pragmatists tolerate him, the average vor v zakone respects him. 

There will be a place for all gangsters... if they have the wit or strength for it. 

On the other hand, Aslan Ûsoyan, the businessman, knows his truth: the Thief and the civvie can never be equal. The Kurdish Spider's financial webs have been built up through the regions, each vibration of his business's webbing giving Aslan more and more confidence in his power. If Ioselani wants each gang on its own, Aslan shall have their powers under him. If Ioselani wants civilians to join the ranks, Aslan will not tolerate the farm animal joining the farmer. 

If everyone is a thief, no one is.

title: Jaba's Last Bow
desc:
The Great Pakhan stared boredly at the gun barrels pointed at him, Usoyan entering his office behind the group of soldiers that came in first. 

"It's over," Usoyan noted, his hands interlocked behind his back. "Jaba, no one's coming." 

Ioseliani yawned demonstratively. "No one, as in-" 

"No one. Your men are all gone. Surrender." Usoyan responded almost mechanically. 

Ioseliani would sigh and stand up from his armchair, ignoring the clicks of the rifles pointed at him. 

"I got a weapon."  

Usoyan blinked at the Great Pakhan's statement, "Pardon?" 

"I got a weapon," Ioseliani smirked at the soldiers' change in demeanour, many getting nervous and grasping their rifles tighter. 

"No, you don't..." Usoyan could generally see where this was going. 

"Oh yes, I do! I got a weapon! I got a-!" Suddenly, Ioseliani's hand would dart into his jacket's inside pocket. 

BANG! BANG! BANG! 

The Great Pakhan fell back, sagging into his armchair, the blood beginning to mix with the whisky seeping from the bullet hole in the flask he reached into his jacket for. 

Usoyan grimaced as the soldiers lowered their rifles. "What a fucking mess..."

title: The Death of a Salesman
desc:
For a day so bright and sunny, it was awfully cold in Aslan's prison cell. Not that he would know, of course. 

The moment it was clear that Aslan Usoyan was not going to win out in his little power struggle with Ioseliani, he, alongside the last remaining pakhans on his side, were rounded up and thrown in a Tyumen jailhouse. Usoyan himself had been sitting in a rotting cell for about four hours, after being abducted earlier that morning. He was still wearing his suit. 

As Usoyan tried and failed to figure out what exactly went wrong, and how Jaba had managed to pull off such a maneuver, the lock on his cell was fiddled with, then finally hit several times, before finally being unlocked. The door opened, letting in quite a bit of sunlight from holes in the bombed-out jail's roof, which blinded Usoyan momentarily. Once his eyes adjusted, he was met with an odd, but not altogether surprising sight; just as he had been there to see the ends of his foreign opponents, Jaba Ioseliani himself had come to end this conflict once and for all. 

"Aslan, young boy!" Jaba greeted his rival, with a smile, "Looks like you've lost this one." Ioseliani picked Usoyan up off of the squalid floor and pulled him out of the cell. His smile faded, and, with a stern gaze Aslan had never seen on the man, led the man through the halls of the old jail. 

When the two of them finally left the building, Aslan could barely contain his horror; every single one of his co-conspirators, a list hundreds of people long, had been lined up along the side of the jail. From the looks of it, an entire Yugran battalion was there, too, Kalashnikovs at the ready. The end had finally come for their plans. 

Usoyan was put at the end of the line, closest to the entrance, where he stood next to a stout man in thug's clothes. Looking at him, as well as many of the other men in the line, Usoyan realized that he didn't even know most of these people. Yet, here they were, about to die for him. Once everyone was firmly in line, Ioseliani ordered his men to line up across from the prisoners, with one soldier to every captive. The "Load!", "Prime!", and "Ready!" orders came a lot faster than Usoyan was hoping for, but it was an awfully long time before he heard "Fire!". 

As the bullet went through his head, his last thoughts were of his mother.

title: The Fuck-It List
desc:
"Gazmanov?" "Fuck 'em." 

"Kamchatski?" "Fuck 'em." 

"Abasdze?" "Fuck 'em." 

Ioseliani threw a knife, hitting a perfect bulls-eye on the dart-board, while Rafael read off the names of Usoyan's cronies and noted down the 'death orders' that the Great Pakhan pronounced as easily as he pronounced a swear. 

"You sure about Abasdze?"  

Ioseliani paused as he took out another knife, turning to his right-hand man with a disgruntled expression. 

"Now, why would I be unsure, Raf, hm?" 

Rafael gulped, "I didn't mean anything behind it, just saying, the guy has connections to the Georgian-" 

Ioseliani cut Rafael off with a lifted hand, "Raf, I said we are going snake hunting, right?" 

"R-right..." 

"Well then, why are you giving this so much fucking thought, hm? Sure, a snake can be a very good decoration, especially if it's exotic, but why should I keep a venomous son of a bitch and risk getting bit when I can tear the fucker's head off!? HM!? RAF!" 

The right-hand man gave a nervous huff. "L-look, all I'm saying, we shouldn't go full Bukharin on this. Y'know, let's not shoot ourselves in the leg just because they don't align with us-" 

"It's a war, Raf, and there's no quarter given or taken. Now, either man the fuck up and keep reading, or get the fuck out." Ioseliani turned back to the dartboard, flicking another knife at it, the blade hitting the hilt of the previous dagger and bouncing off. 

The Great Pakhan continued, "We leave one Usoyan crony, he'll sprout two more, two will turn into four, and soon his business bullshit will be all over us again." 

"..." 

"So? Continue!" 

"Right, Ibrahem?"

title: A Little Assistance
desc:
"The Far East metal? That's all they want?" Usoyan hummed a little. "The Japanese are certainly cheap." 

Ilo stood near his commander, side-eyeing the contracts they had received in huge bundles, the Kurdish Spider now having sat for several hours, staring over the demands that came with the aid. 

"Well..." Usoyan stamped the document, one of many dozen he had already gone through. "Their equipment will carry us if ours won't." 

Ilo cleared his throat. "Maybe take a look at the American letters? I think that there were a few quite simple ones."  

"Certainly, certainly." Usoyan pulled one of the sheets, before snorting and taking out a blank piece of paper and writing something on it. 

"Sir?" 

Usoyan handed the two sheets back to Ilo, chuckling. "There, send them this. It should work." 

"If it isn't too much, what exactly-" 

"Oh, nothing actually impactful,"

title: Business Restructuring
desc:
Rafael felt a sense of deja vu, sighing as he read off the new list of names, noting down Ioseliani's new orders. 

"Gurgenidze..." 

"Hmmmmm... Minister of the Interior." 

"Voronov..." 

"Ah, that prick, stick him into the Ministry of Agriculture, somewhere at the bottom. Let's make him eat shit." 

"Dekanosidze..." 

"Well, he's quite a good officer. I think he deserves a good time in Financing." Ioseliani, who had up to then been leaning back in his chair, would sit forward and stretch, yawning. 

Rafael looked at the time. "It is quite late in the night, Jaba. Maybe we should finish tomorrow." 

Ioseliani lifted his eyes in a tired manner, "Right, gimme a run-down of the remaining candidates." 

Rafael quickly eyed the list. "Some Georgians who sided with you over Usoyan and a Russian officer who crossed lines and flipped to our side." 

The Great Pakhan stood from his seat, picking up the bottle on the table and headed towards the exit, "Stuff them somewhere in the Military Office and the Russian can go into Agricultural low-levels as well." 

Rafael blinked, pronouncing nervously, "Jaba, maybe we should rethink this... are we not rushing things?" 

Ioseliani turned his head, the door to the dark outside already opened, giving his right-hand man a disgruntled look, "Well, if they're gonna be loyal,"

options.name: "Who gives a shit where they are?"

title: Highway Robbery!
desc:
Within the interlocking mechanisms and struggles of the Thief State, the resistance between Great Pakhan Ioseliani and Aslan Usoyan have exploded! A recent caravan of Usoyan supply-runners has disappeared for several days. Upon mounting a search, the trucks and the bodies of the drivers were found, or rather, whatever remained of them. From the official investigation, it is known that the caravan has been attacked mid-drive, all of the drivers that survived the initial attack were executed by bayonets, and the trucks were found to have been emptied before the attackers got away. 

The event has caused an uproar within the Circle, many accusing Ioseliani's forces of a lack of oversight over his men and some even accusing the Great Pakhan of giving a direct order for the assault, while many others blame Usoyan for a possible false flag operation, considering the light load of the trucks compared to the usual transports or a possible assault on the Thief's army as many drivers were found to be armed.

options.name: No one is innocent, everyone is guilty...

title: Usoyan corrupts our administration!
desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 11:14 PM; 

This month's financial report has had an unfortunate discovery; multiple high-level bureaucrats and underlings have started to receive considerable amounts of money from obfuscated accounts. Further investigation revealed the accounts to secretly belong to various accountants and analysts in the employ of Aslan Usoyan. The accounts have been shut down, but there isn't enough evidence to arrest anyone, and it won't be long before they simply open new accounts. 

OPINION: Usoyan's webs seem to be more intricate than we previously believed. Although we delayed them from paying out our men in the name of getting them on Aslan's side, you can probably guess this won't stop them very much at all. Us Kurds have to be crafty to survive, these days, but Usoyan seems to supersede "crafty" with moves like these. We have to get a grip on our men if we want to stay in power. 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.

options.name: Start an investigation, we need to uncover everything.

title: Usoyan sways our allies!
desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 6:41 PM; 

 After a routine inspection, several more thieves-in-law than before were found with documents, pins, and other pieces of evidence suggesting that they are loyal to our rival, Aslan Usoyan. It appears a series of bribes, threats, and ideological conversions continue to move our men under Usoyan's thrall. Counteraction is recommended at this time. 

OPINION: "Usoyan got the drop on us; more of our underlings and officials have gone to his side. If we want to end this power struggle, we need to keep everyone we can on our side, not let our opponents steal people right from under our noses. I know I'm meant to be your informant, but it doesn't bring me much confidence to see these sorts of things happen." 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Mr. Usoyan's secretary as of writing this, 

Leonid Rojov

options.name: Blackmail everyone involved, I won't surround myself with snakes.

title: Usoyan's propaganda sways the people!
desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 9:30 AM; 

Last night, Aslan Usoyan's underlings posted up hundreds of posters throughout several of out major cities; posters either painting Aslan as a hero of the people whose reforms would make Russia great, or condemning Jaba Ioseliani as a complacent, greedy man who wishes to steal from the Russian people. Although the veracity of these posters is, at the very least, up for debate, thousands of people have seen it, and only a couple dozen have been vandalized or taken down in response. 

OPINION: Although it is difficult to gauge the popularity of political posters, especially in an environment where many are scared of those that put them up, just how many of them are still up, as well as the more likely still being put up, makes this move a resounding success on the part of Usoyan. The time to make our own move comes closer and closer, and our move must be swift and a bit more than decisive. 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.

options.name: Tear everything down, no more people should see this.

desc:
Extract from 'Utro' Gazette: 

...while investigation into the incident is still on-going, several gunmen have been wounded during the attack on {ILLEGIBLE} Square. Several dozen bystanders were caught in the fire of the terrorists, including women and children. The city has been put under lockdown. The editorials condolences go out to the families of the victims...

desc:

title: Usoyan sways the people!
desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 9:30 AM; 

Yesterday morning, Usoyan was seen making a public appearance, a considerable crowd of people was listening to his speech. Promises of freedom, wealth and greatness were made by the Kurd, making a huge part of those in attendance flock to his banner, or cease support of our power base. 

OPINION: Well, there's nothing too special about this move, the best we can do is answer by heading our own public campaign, and considering your charisma, it shouldn't be too difficult of a task. 

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.

title: Usoyan receives foreign investments!
desc:
SITUATION REPORT: 9:30 AM; 

These last days our spies detected an influx of anomalous investments from foreign businessmen into Thief subsidiaries. After some digging, we managed to track down the sudden source of liquidity, the capital was passed to façade companies whose owners were only name bearers. Upon further investigation and "convincing" of the company holders, we discovered that most of these shells track back to Usoyan. Wherever that funding goes is not certain, but it doesn't look like it's beneficial to the state apparatus.

OPINION: Sir, this is proof that our economic laws are flawed, these evident loopholes can be used by enemies of the state to smuggle in funds from outside our territory. We could make use for some regulation.

SIGNED: Your friend, and Aslan Usoyan's secretary as of writing, 

Leonid Rojov.

title: Usoyan hijacks our communications!
desc:
Yesterday the Great Pakhan guard has warned that there was a breach of security in the military outpost *REDACTED*. As of now, we were able to confirm that the perpetrators stole the frequencies and ciphers that the military uses for communications. We do not know exactly how much the Usoyani loyalists managed to gain from our conversations, but all communications for the several weeks are to be considered compromised and the ciphers are to be re-written. 

OPINION: "Now THIS will prove to be a real problem, sir. The best course of action is to cut all communications on the leaked frequencies and remake our cipher books. At least for the coming week, I believe our command structure is partially paralysed."

title: Terrorist Attack Repelled!
desc:
Today, a potential attack on our installation on *REDACTED* street has been preemptively halted, with the effort of several officers and back-up patrols all the assailants were either arrested or disposed of. Most of the signs and the accounts we were to beat out of the arrested point to this being organised by Usoyan. This failure will likely discredit him, at least for the time being. 

OPINION: "A close shave, a very close one, we should higher the security of *REDACTED* just to be safe. Considering that the weapons generally match some of those missing 'in transport' from factories, I also suggest to investigate the state apparatus further."

title: The Fool's Speech
desc:

A recent speech by famed business magnate Aslan Usoyan has come under fire from both the Circle and the general public. While having his speech dismissed in the Circle as 'babble', the reaction to the same speech was much more violent from the people in the streets as Mister Usoyan was pelted with rocks, only with the arrival of the local security forces ending the violent attack.

title: Ioseliani executes our loyalists!
desc:
SITREP: 06:03 

Reports have come in from several of our contacts that last night, no less than two dozen men sympathetic, if not loyal, to our cause were taken forcibly from their homes, put on a bus, and taken out to a forest outside Tyumen, where they were apparently lined up and shot. At least one of our contacts was forced to shoot several men, many of whom knew him as an ally. Our popular support is already starting to stagnate as news of this event spreads. 

OPINION: Really? Just... taken and shot? Like dogs? This sort of thing cannot happen again if we want even one person to work with us. ...By the way, you should really read these Mario Fusco books. You could learn a lot from the main character; for example, he wouldn't let his friends be rounded up like cattle. 

SIGNED: Your loyal secretary and countryman, 

Leonid Rojov.

title: Ioseliani stabilizes the government!
desc:

The meetings also either dissuaded or "dissuaded" them from working with us. Due to the apparent success of these meetings, several pakhans and officials have either left our circles or cut off recruitment contact. 

OPINION: It appears Ioseliani figured out how to stabilize the government, or at least convince people the government is stable. This tactic has already lost us some good men, and we need to step up our efforts if we want any hope of victory. 

SIGNED: Your loyal secretary and countryman, 

Leonid Rojov.

Maybe the speeches were all the same, but this time it didn't seem to work.
