title: An Unpleasant Surprise
desc:
Heinrich Himmler looked at the many forms on his desk.  Since Degrelle's disappearance, it had seemed that further threats to his Ordenstaat were falling one by one. Grabbing the next sheet of paper, he signed another execution order for some French traitor.  A shame, really. So many useful people kept getting themselves killed. It wasn't that hard to understand the supremacy of the Aryan, was it? Why would someone align themselves with such inferior beliefs? 

His thoughts were interrupted by the knock of a junior SS officer on the door.  

"Come in." 

"Mein Reichsführer," the young bureaucrat mumbled nervously, as he handed a thick folder, stamped "STRENG GEHEIM: NUR FÜR DIE AUGEN DES REICHSFÜHRERS", to the most dangerous man in France.  "It seems that..." 

"Speed it up, boy, I'm not mad at you, no need to be so formal. Yet." 

With the scolding clearly heard on his face, the officer handed Himmler the folder. Himmler walked back to his desk, unclasping the hinge and taking out what looked to be the largest report he had ever received. It dwarfed even the most verbose of Ribbentrop's dossiers, before the dolt got himself killed. 

As he read, however, it was clear why it was so long. 

The report detailed what was probably the most absurd, pathetic, and horrible thing that had ever happened within his domain. If what was written was true, the country had quite literally been robbed by Russian bandits. 

A young Yugran agent, who happened to know German well enough to pass off as Flemish, had climbed up the barbed, electrified, and heavily guarded border fence, snuck into the country, and had slowly infiltrated the Walloonian Legion. Eventually, the subhuman broke into a nuclear silo, put the highly radioactive warhead into a derelict suitcase, and hopped the border back into Germany. 

Why why why why why why why why WHY.  

Himmler began shaking. Very visibly. 

"You're telling me that some Russian criminal worm crossed the greatest border the world has ever seen, snuck into a nuclear missile silo, and managed to WALK out of here with one of our nukes? As if we were dimwitted Bolsheviks?"  

There was no reply. 

"I want the that silo's commander head removed off his fucking shoulders. Is that understood?" 

"Y-yes, my Reichsführer." 

"Now get the fuck out of my office!"

title: Past Prides
desc:
Jaba Ioseliani took a good look at his new dacha as he got out of the banya.  Ironically located in the idyllic woods outside of Omsk of all places, it was luxuriously decorated and a far cry from the usual pre-war cottages most had for summer homes.  He slid into the cold lake, the shock of the frigid ice water waking his whole body.  Life was good, he thought to himself.  After all, he was lucky to even be alive. 

The escape from the Vorkuta gulags was tough enough.  That bastard Blokhin acted like the Union had never fallen, working him and his fellow thieves to the bone.  He laughed a little thinking about the look on Vasily's face when it was the thieves throwing him into prison to rot.  

Oh, those early years were nothing but struggle.  Stalin, Rokossovsky, Yazov, Batov, the names flew through his head.  They were all stronger, their armies fierce remnants of the Old Union while he could only call upon a ragtag militia of thieves.  But the Thieves were stronger in the end. They always were because those generals and politicians could never understand that when the going gets tough, it's cunning that wins out. 

And now, the wolves were feasting.  His realm stretched from the border with German-occupied Russia to the expanse of Central Siberia to his east.  The Thieves were no longer a tired band of escaped prisoners, and Ioseliani wasn't just the Great Pakhan.  He was meant to be the leader of all Russia.  The realization shocked him more than the freezing waters.  As he pulled himself out of the lake and went back inside to dry off, he realized, now more than ever, that all of Russia was his for the taking.  He couldn't shy away from it now.

title: Back to Business
desc:
Levon breathed heavily, his weight put against the wall, his back hunched over as he tried to keep his gastric juices down, gagging at the sight in front of him. "W-WHAT THE FUCK!?"  

Patunin, on the other hand, looked at the body with a cold disconnection. "Well, Leva, get the bag from the motorcycle." The ex-militsioner observed the scene, noting the boot sizes and the position of the beaten and broken cadaver in front of them. The remains of the ex-komissar in front of them had been kicked and stoned to death by some gang or other, and Patunin supposed that the only reason HE wasn't in that place himself was how unforgivingly corrupt he has been his whole life.  

The younger man tried to straighten out and walk, before groaning and nearly dropping to his knees, his breakfast almost spilling onto the asphalt.  

The ex-policeman sighed, walking up to Levan, patting his back, "Come on, Leva! They handed you over from the Army, you gotta have seen at least a FEW bodies-" 

"Goh... Papanya, you don't see this kinda stuff in the army- HURP-" As the younger man's words were cut off, Patunin jumped back to avoid getting his shoes painted by vomit and swore under his breath. 

First, he was a gumshoe, but after he hit his prime, the promotion finally came and the cushy job rolled in with it, until they figured out where all those finances went that is. Several years in the gulag, and now he was back to THIS... Only that he was serving with the same men he shared a cell with not so long ago. 

"Fucking hell..." Pulling Levon up by the elbow, he would drag him out to the motorcycle, propping his 'protege' up against the sidecar and taking the 'police'-issued potato sack to put the corpse in. 

"Catch your breath, Alisa said they found more like this, so we have a long day ahead."

title: Providence/stay
desc:
"The what now?" Lukov lifted an eyebrow questioningly at his son and took a sip of his Sunday morning coffee. In the end, the fried exotic beans were still an expensive commodity, so treating himself once a week was the most he could do. 

"Providence/stay! They show it on TV after the news!" Oleg was quite smart for a twelve-year-old, the pair of glasses Lukov smuggled in for the adopted orphan causing the boy's grades to 'suddenly' jump, but considering how he hoped his adopted son would grow up, the rugged bandit was a little disappointed. "It's gonna start in ten minutes! Let's watch!" 

"Alyosha... Are you not a bit too old for cartoons?" While Lukov tried to phrase the absent-mindedly spoken phrase without any offence, the boy's enthusiasm would suddenly extinguish.  

"O-oh, s-sorry, right..." The boy would lower his head a little. 

Lukov sighed, "Well, considering how well you've been in school, maybe I was a little harsh." The bandit placed down his mug. "Let's go watch together for a bit, hm?" 

Oleg would perk up, "Right! You're gonna love it!" He would grab the man's hand, pulling him towards the living room of their shabby apartment, "It's got this school guy who fights against historical figures and, like, they gotta fight until only one is left to reclaim-"  

Lukov rolled his eyes a little, quickly getting lost in his son's incomprehensible explanation of the plot, but coming along anyways and sitting in front of the TV. 

With a click, the screen lit up. 

"It's already started!" 

Lukov did not really get why the proportions of the characters were so bizarre, big eyes, colourful hair but aside from the crude shapes, one thought occupied the back of his mind...

options.name: "Christ, what are the kids even watching these days..."
"Not too bad, maybe Oleg's onto something..."

title: Lawful Crookery
desc:
"Jaba!" Ivan burst through the door, the letter of forced resignation still in his hand. "Jaba! You bastard! You cannot do this to m-" 

Ioseliani would open his eyes, yawning lazily and standing from his armchair, stretching slightly. 

"Are you listening to me!? This is bullshit! THIS IS FUCKING BULLSHIT! I SERVED YOU WELL AND GOOD! I-" 

 POW! 

Ivan fell back, his jaw giving way to the Great Pakhan's knuckles with a sickening crack, the ex-officer giving a pitiful howl and holding onto his face as his ears rang. 

"You enter into my office," Ioseliani kicked him in the ribs, "Wake me the fuck up," Another kick, another terrified grunt, "And tell me I CANNOT DO SOMETHING THAT'S WRITTEN IN THE THIEF'S LAW, YOU LITTLE RUNT!" The last kick would cause Ivan to roll over on his back now holding on to both his face, blood running from his mouth and nose, the punch having made good contact. 

Jaba would lean forward, "By the Thief Laws, your actions at Vorkuta in aiding the Usoyani forces are to be considered TREACHERY, and it doesn't matter if it was BEFORE sides were chosen, so, you little fucking mongrel, don't you fucking DARE disturb my nap with your yapping when you are a clear cut traitor..." 

Ioseliani grinned, "By law, you are a nobody, got it? Not a Thief anymore... But I also did it because I fucking hate you, Ivan, and I always hated you." 

Ivan would try to scramble back only to receive a kick to the face, blood droplets hitting the floor.  

"Who gave you the right to even CONSIDER a place as a general? You were always uppity." Ioseliani spit on the floor, turning around and walking back to his armchair. 

"Alright, now get the fuck out of my sight before I blow your brains out, filthy traitor." The last part was said with a pleased demonstrative close of the eyes.

options.name: Laws are written to be abused.

title: There's Always a Bigger Dog
desc:
Artur Cohen sighed and rubbed his hands, trying to ease his nervousness. He never had the chance to return to teaching after the war had failed. No, he barely had time to save himself, to run further East, hiding his Jewish roots. 

"She just ran into my fist!" The girls in front of his desk were both students, both of them on the way to graduation. While he could not remember the name of the first one off the top of his head, the little mutt that stood to the right of her, her name he knew VERY well. Sofia Berezovskaya. 

The daughter of the local Pakhan snickered self-indulgently. "I said, SHE RAN INTO MY FIST, YOU OLD OWL!"  

Cohen considered standing up and grabbing the little bitch by the ear. 'Ran into her fist', what utter bollocks, this generation knew nothing about discipline, let alone simple empathy. 'Old owl', if he was still in the Union, she would be on cleaning duty for the next decade for insulting a teacher! 

Then his mind jumped to her father. If the principal disciplined her, what was next? Berezovskiy did not need to send an army to Cohen's door. It was simple. His papers would start 'getting lost' in the bureaucracy, the school's investors would all suddenly pull out for various reasons, local businesses would serve him badly or not serve him at all. 

"Is that true, Masha?"  

The girl with the black eye would sniffle and nod. Cohen ground his teeth but opened his mouth. 

"Then there is no more problem, return to classes." 

As the two left, Sofia would shove Masha through the door, giggling. Cohen sat back in his chair and rubbed his face. No, he would never have had the chance to rebuild a school before the Thieves came in.

title: Along the South
desc:
Ioseliani felt a sense of deja vu, as he walked into the room of generals, all of them around the map of Russia as Batov continued explaining something in a focused manner, the only light being the huge lamp in the centre of the room as it shone on every crease of the paper. 

"Planning the march East, eh?" The Great Pakhan took a swig from his bottle, walking up to the table, the generals parting to let him through, leaving only Batov standing on the opposite side of the table. 

"We certainly are." Batov responded absent-mindedly, tracing his finger on the Eastern front. 

"So, old boy, what do you have for me?" Ioseliani kicked a chair to the table, sitting down and taking on his usual bored expression. 

Batov lifted his eyes. "Well, for starters we have some good understanding of the enemy's industry centres." He traced his finger on the southern border. "The Northern climate makes it hard for any city to develop well, so going too far North, or committing more forces there will probably result in resource starvation and useless land." 

"So what do you propose?" Ioseliani had by now gotten used to Batov's self-centred style of explanation. The General knew what he was doing when it came to strategy and tended to get wrapped up in his own thoughts, the Great Pakhan just had to listen. 

Batov smiled, his eyes still on the map. "Either we use overwhelming forces to crush the clearly less-protected north and encircle the heavily armed south, or we utilize Omsk as a shield to exhaust them." 

Ioseliani grinned, getting up. "It seems you have it under control." While the phrase seemed to be directed at the whole group of generals, Batov could swear he had seen a respectful nod towards himself as the Great Pakhan departed.

options.name: Never disturb a great craftsman in his labour.

title: Greed Conquers All
desc:
Otto nervously scratched the back of his head, the aged administrator rubbing his hands as the two men in the worn SS uniforms observed the warhead that was snuck out through the service tunnels, the greyed man in a lab coat that came with them checking some parts and pieces, the Geiger counter in his hand picking up small disturbances. 

"I-is everything up to expectation?" The two men turned their heads at Otto's inquiry, one of them chuckling, while the third one continued checking the warhead. 

The nearest man in the SS uniform, the blonde, as if he came straight off of a propaganda poster, turned back to the lab-coated individual pronouncing something in Russian, Otto grimacing at the Untermensch language. 

The 'professor' lifted his head, turning off the Geiger counter and nodding. 

The blonde turned back to the administrator, sighing and unbuttoning the black jacket, Otto feeling a freezing block of ice drop into his stomach. Was he a loose end to them..? 

"P-please I have a wife, sh-she's sick, I swear it's the real thi-" The blonde came up to Otto at a leisurely pace, reaching for something in the inside jacket pocket, "P-please..." 

A stack of papers was stuffed into his hands, the administrator pausing, terror changing to surprise. 

"Shut the fuck up. Two passports to Switzerland, two 'mill' dollars on the offshore account," The blonde pronounced with a deep Russian accent, grinning. "Now fuck off, Papasha, deal is done." 

Otto wiped away the drop of cold sweat as the three turned to the nuclear-laden truck, boarding it to depart back to whatever Untermensch hellhole they were from, several joking in-between each other and laughing as they went.

options.name: Not even the Aryan man can withstand the call of Capital.

title: The Shadow State
desc:
Stepan had Volga German roots, however, in the end, the only thing that mattered was that he could speak German and had blonde hair. You wouldn't be able to get a more 'Aryan' Slav if you combed through the whole of Europe. And the Yugran bandits could not believe their luck when that 'Aryan' was found in a local bandit. 

On the other hand, Arkadiy did not look Aryan. The smuggler's black hair, brown shifty eyes, and small stature looked nothing like the posters, but in the end, Ost-Paris met the two as warmly as a breezeblock regardless. 

It was early morning, the two have already awakened in the abandoned bunker hidden within the forest floor and pulled on their smuggled SS uniforms, trying their best to not let the anxiety get to them. 

"Stepka, I'm gonna go check what's up-top, you go get the docs, got it?" Stepan nodded, turning to Arkadiy's backpack, the latter would slowly push the rusted trapdoor of the bunker open, peering through the small gap, seeing if any patrol was passing through. 

Silence... 

"I think it's-" Arkadiy would go quiet, as he heard the hurried shuffle of fallen leaves on the ground, but continued observing. 

The Frenchman must have escaped the daily march to the work camp, but the state he was in, it was surprising he could even run, his skin hanging off of him like ill-fit clothing, his eyes sunken into the skull. "Non! Non! S'il vous plait, n-" Arkadiy heard a click somewhere in the distance and- 

"There they are," Stepan finally found the documents turning back to his comrade, only to find the man sitting against the closed bunker trap door, his face ashen. 

"Arka, 'sup with you?" 

"I think..." He mumbled.

options.name: "I think we should wait for a bit..."

title: Providence Didache
desc:
"So what's the show even about?" Vlad still felt, to say the least, sceptical about Kydyr's invitation to watch a cartoon, of all things. 

In return, his bandit friend would sigh and knock some ash off of his cigarette. "Providence lore? I'm pretty sure the fuckers up in the state departments specifically made it impenetrable so that some jackboot fuck can't make sense of it." 

This did not fill Vlad with confidence as he continued to stare blindly into the screen, "Isn't there... a shortened version?" 

Kydyr paused, staring into the box of the smuggled TV, clearly trying to formulate his idea as some weirdly shaped character pummelled another weirdly shaped character. "Well... Okay, imagine every other century a lotta very rich mad fucks get together to fight to the death." 

"Right, so basically pakhans." 

"Yeah, sure, pakhans. A couple of pakhans gather up every other century and fight to the death so that the survivor can get a chance to get a wish granted to them by the Golden Fleece." 

"Aaaand, that's it..?" 

"They also summon some historical figures as their 'companions' in fights. Lotsa magical bullshit. Just roll with it..."  

Vlad was feeling unsure if he wanted to really watch it anymore... 

"So... they summon anyone?" 

"Hm? Oh yeah, Giordano Bruno, Carl Friedrich Wagner, Nevsky, Pushkin, Peter the Great..." 

"Anyone more modern?" 

"Yeah, kinda why I invited you, they're gonna reveal the Great Pakhan's companion form." 

"Companion? Wouldn't they want him to be one of the guys fighting?" 

"It's Providence lore, don't worry about it- Wait there it is!" Kydyr sat forward, "They're summoning him!" 

Vlad also sat forward, "Get outta the way you're blocking the screen!" 

"Oh shush! Lemme-" Kydyr paused, his expression turning to shock... "Gaha... GAHAHAHA!" The bandit fell back, his sides going into orbit from what he just saw. 

Vlad looked at the screen, seeing... a purple-haired... girl..? "W-why's the Great Pakhan a girl..?" He could barely contain the confused disgust in his tone. 

Kydyr sat up wiping his cheeks from the tears of laughter. "Gohoho... Oh man, Vladik, the funniest part-"

title: UNFORGIVABLE
desc:
Rafael carefully stepped into Ioseliani's office, a reflexive nervous gulp travelling down his throat. The room was a complete mess, papers lying around, some of them torn, some of them wet with what looked like whiskey stains, as if a booze-filled whirlwind burst through the room. 

"RAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAF!" The right-hand man finally noticed the Great Pakhan emptying one of the bookcases, looking for something, his usually slicked back hair in tufts, the smell of heavy booze in the air, "GET THE FUCK HERE, YOU SON OF A BITCH!" 

"H-hey, Boss..."  

Ioseliani looked up from the drawer, his eyes bloodshot, Rafael never having seen such an enraged expression on the man before. Standing up, Ioseliani would turn back to emptying the drawers, his jaw clenched. 

"Raf, who in fuck's name had let the Japanese into the propaganda department!?" 

"W-what?" 

The bookshelf would tumble to the floor with a great smash as the Great Pakhan pulled it down, looking around like a trapped beast and continuing his ruffle through the paperwork. 

"I said, WHO LET THE ASIANS INTO THE MOTHERFUCKING PROPAGANDA DEPARTMENT!?" 

Rafael blinked, trying to process. "Is there... a problem..?"  

"Yes! THAT!" Ioseliani pointed at his desk. Rafael would carefully tip-toe around the spilt papers and reach the desk. The only thing left on it was a small figurine of a... bandit? Bandit girl? The proportions were weird, eyes were slightly too big, the limbs a bit too thin, and the hair was... purple? She also seemed to look like a... teen? 

"What am I looking at, Boss?"  

"Their product! Told me they were gonna make a show, something about a good FUCKING IMAGE! GOOD IMAGE, MY BA-" Ioseliani pulled out the paper, slurring out a victorious 'Ah-ha!'. 

"OUT OF THE WAY, RAF! AND IF I SEE YOU TAKE THAT FIGURINE, YOU WILL REGRET IT FOR THE REST OF YOUR SHORT LIFE! NONE ON THIS LIST WILL LIVE TO SEE TOMORROW!" Ioseliani would burst out of the room, taking out his revolver as he went, the thing almost misfiring into his leg, leaving the right-hand man in shocked silence.

title: A Long Way From Home
desc:
Usoyan sat at his desk, his fingers interlocked, the freezing night howling powerlessly against the glass of his window, the oil lamp casting a warm glow across his office. In such moments, he would cast his mind to the past, the Old World's siren call pulling him back 

Tbilisi, 24 years old, young and inexperienced, the next thing he knew one of the pigs had grabbed him and beat him into submission. Stealing didn't give him much, and the short death row did not reform him, but it sure as Hell taught him a lot about life. 

Aslan allowed himself a thoughtful scowl as he stared into the flickering flames. The Tiflis Three were strange beasts in his eyes. On one hand, their deaths got his jailers' heads torn off, on the other hand, while he may have escaped, his homeland lay under the same monster that ruined it since he was a child.  

When the jail guards got called off to fight, it did not take long to overpower the green boys they put up instead, and then he ran... Oh he ran, he sure did. Trekking across the Caucasus, further North, past the constantly changing warlord borders, with fake names and faker currency, meeting many, remembering few. 

Usoyan shook off the nostalgia, but as his hand reached to extinguish the flame of the lamp, muttered,"Tbiliso, mzis da vardebis mkhareo..."

options.name: "Tbilisi, the side of sun and roses..."

title: Creeping Roots
desc:
"The fuck do you mean we gotta answer for every bullet!?" Valygin almost spat with rage as he slammed his rifle on the desk. 

Xatun put down the smuggled porno mag, his expression showing that he would rather be anywhere but here, explaining to some mook why the arsenal started to keep tabs. 

"Valygin, tell me, do you get paid?" 

"Well, yeah, since last month." 

"Right, so no more random looting raids. That also means that instead of letting you blockheads take any weapons and ammunition you like, we gotta collect it, mark it, sell it off..." 

"Right..." Valygin made a thinking face, Xatun continuing the logical chain. 

"So that we can buy ammo for YOUR guns, because you work for the Territory, right? And if we buy you ammo, instead of you taking it, whose ammo is it?" 

Valygin clenched his jaw.  

Xatun noticed the spark of understanding, "That's right, it's not YOUR ammo, it's OUR ammo, and if you're using OUR ammo, you're BORROWING it, you blockhead! Every time you chamber a round, that's territory budget getting fired through those skulls. And what do we do with money if we're not using it?" 

The bandit soldier sighed dejectedly, "We count it." 

"Good job, Valygin, maybe you're not completely mentally deficient! Now get out and stop bothering me,"

options.name: "Last time I heard, they'll be counting rifles soon."

title: The Unbreakables
desc:
"You look older, Diyar." Aslan noted, looking at his men unloading the trucks of equipment in the distance, the smog of the early morning factories starting up making the machines look like giant bugs. 

"And your Kurdi is rusty, brother. None of us are getting younger." Diyar took out a pack of cigarettes, putting one between his lips, Usoyan grimacing and looking away. 

"I simply wanted to offer you an exit, if you need it. I got myself land in the Russian Wastes, you can walk out of this and-" 

"And leave the sunny lands of the 'Black State' behind?" The grey-haired man lit his cigarette chuckling as he puffed on it. 

Usoyan's scowl only grew, "This cause, our cause, it's-" 

"Save your breath, brother, you'll just breathe more smog. You can tell me about how terrible Kaukasien is as much as you want, it won't matter considering I live it." Diyar would stand up, wiping his hands on the camouflage pants. 

"Georgia wasn't all great, being that to them we were not their own. But in the end, this fight, it's not just for us, brother." The old man pulled the strap of the machine gun over his shoulder, taking a few more puffs of his cigarette. 

"This isn't about being Kurdish, or Georgian, or hating the Germans. Men had stood and died to set us free again, the Tiflis Three let not one single scream when they hoisted them up. So," Diyar turned back to Usoyan. "How am I to run away when the fight is just warming up, with your guns and all?" 

"I... I do not know." Usoyan swapped his speech from Kurdi to Georgian, the older man, in turn, looking away before giving him a slap on the shoulder and grinning.  

"The fight is not over, Aslan. Not with you on our side. We will be free, brother. Just you watch us. Now go,"

options.name: "Your path in Russia awaits you, just as mine awaits me here."

title: Vultures
desc:
As the piggish mining executives argued over which parts of Russia they would rip open when the reunification is complete, Aslan realized that he truly, supremely did not care for these people. The Germans and the Japanese were more likely to use slave labor than hire Russians, and the Americans would probably underpay them. His thoughts were interrupted, however, by the first demands of the meeting; those of the large Reichswerke HG man. 

"Alright, Mr. Usoyan, we've looked over the geological data here, and..."began the man, before trailing off. His Russian was subpar. "...and we would like to mine here," he pointed out on their map as he spoke, "here, and here." He pointed to three hillside areas near the Moskowein-Russian border. With a disillusioned, if still loyal and dogmatic voice, he continued, "The Reich requests that you generously give us the mining rights for those three sites. The oil and other resources there are requested by the Reichstag itself," 

"It will be considered, my friend," Usoyan replied, as cordially as he could, for such a man, "However, I would still like to hear from the others before I make any final decision. Mr. Davenport, from Freeport McMoRan?" With his words, the American, a lean man obviously high on cocaine, stood, and pointed to a spot on the Kamchatka peninsula. 

"It says here that diamond and borax deposits center at this point, where my finger is? We wanna mine right there, yeah. You'll let us?" 

"Again, my friend, we must hear the requests of all parties," Usoyan replied, with more control than with the German, "Mr. Aso, you actually run the mining company you represent, what do you wish to mine?" Takakishi Aso, head of the Aso mining company, rather than pointing on the map, began his request; 

"There's a hill near the Manchurian border, one with a yellowish scar on its side. We wish to run our mine on that hill, which is located..." He pointed to a hill on the map, some 290 kilometers away from the border, "...right there." 

Usoyan stood for a moment, giving the appearance of deep thought. However, the mining operations were far from his thoughts; of course these people could mine there, even the Germans! They had no clue how much money they were going to make him. He finally answered; 

"Gentlemen, you have the permission of our organization to mine where you have each requested. The Reich, the Sphere, and the free world will have their mines." With those words, Usoyan walked out, and several underlings rushed to each of the executives, giving them dozens of forms and paperwork to sign. 

For the first time in a while, Usoyan smiled.

title: Just Business
desc:
"Prost!" Abs lifted the champagne glass, gnawing on his usual cigar, his little eyes darting from one company man to another, a knowing grin trudging up to his lips. 

"Prest!" Flick slurred, the corporation leader certainly had too many whiskies, his usual fiery temper now flickering in all directions like a flame in a strong wind, the glass between his fingers in a very unsure position. 

"Prost." Geilenberg looked the most modest of them all, the glass of German beer being quite symbolic for the state-corporation puppet. 

"Certainly!" Siemens even stood up a little, his glass of wine held with a steady hand, but his cheeks slightly red, the old man also having relaxed with the coming of alcohol. 

"And to the destruction of those fu-!" Flick opened his mouth, about to go on another rant. 

"Yes yes, Friedrich, 'the lesser races', but let the guest of honour speak first." Abs interrupted, stopping the situation from devolving further, curiously waiting for the last corporation leader to raise a toast. 

Usoyan grimaced as he looked at his new business partners, and picked up his glass of water, uninterested in alcohol. 

"Well, gentlemen, I suppose, prost." 

Abs was almost glimmering, "To future success!"

title: Time for a rebrand
desc:
Air was filled with cigar smoke. Radio played old, slow music while Usoyan sat in his office, looking outside the window. He spectated the scene outside, soldiers marching towards their duties, while on street people walked around, going to their jobs or going home. He had a big proud smile on his face. He ruled them all, high above the others in a way he only dreamed of as a boy.

 His calm was broken as someone knocked at the door. "Come in!" Usoyan shouted as he turned around to face the doors. It was Devdari, his right hand man.  "Everything is ready Sir. We are waiting for you to arrive."

"Ah Devdari, my good old Devdari..." He said while lighting up another cigar."You see all this? Do you see what we hold in our hand? This power that...some leaders would be able just to dream about?" He got up from a chair."After all these years of fighting... it is time for a big move, for a big centralization. It is time to rebrand our company." As he finished his little speech, he proceeded to the meeting that Devdari informed him about.

options.name: A toast to our future investments

title: Our biggest venture
desc:
Usoyan, dressed in all formals with a proud smile, headed towards the conference room. As he entered the room, all politicians and generals sitting at the table stood up, greeting him with respect. He sat at the head of the table. Silence spread through the room, with only the sound of papers moving being heard.

"Gentlemen!" he said, clearing his throat,"I think it's finally a time for us to speak about our opponents in Siberia. Our mighty state grew stronger over the recent period of time, and we can - we should - start preparing for the war that I see as the biggest one yet! But, we must not underestimate our opponents, who used these years to build up their own military and industry, thus posing a big threat to us. But let us not be discouraged by that sight - we will crush not only our most immediate adversaries, but every other madman that would dare to stand in our way towards the final and utmost conquest of all Russian lands!"

A small comotion appeared as he made a pause in his speech. Some people didn't accept it well, while others looked at him with a more or less well-hidden smile. Whispers filled the room, slightly breaking the silence. Then Usoyan continued talking.

"Gentlemen, I hereby advise that we immediately start preparing ourselves for the upcoming storm. We need our factories pumping out more guns, our men tough as steel, our generals ready to lead these same men into the battle! This said, the meeting is over. The fate of this country rests upon your shoulders, so don't screw this up." After a brief moment of silence, Usoyan stood up and left the room with a quick step. The rest of the men present remained there for another couple of minutes, discussing what they just heard.

options.name: "This is going to be tough, my friend!"

title: The Wasteland Economy
desc:
Sashka screamed as his comrade's head exploded from the sniper fire, falling backwards, feeling the burn of stomach acid rise up to the back of his throat as he felt the taste of copper in his mouth, blinded by the crimson on his face. 

"Vadim! God! VADIM!" His panicked shout was cut short with another shot, the spark of his mind going out permanently as half of his skull came off with the speed of the flying round, slumping onto the snow and staining it with red. 

The spotter, Catherine, would get out of cover first, followed by Arseniy, the two walking in utter silence, approaching the dead men. 

"Check his pockets first. Looks like an officer." The bandit girl followed the sniper's orders and would lean down, beginning to riffle through what was Vadim's pockets. 

"Anything? Don't like being so far in the open." 

"No, just usual communist threads and crumbs. Some ciggies though..." Catherine would take out an intricate metal cigar case, refurbished for holding shitty papirosa cigarettes, and flip it open, noticing the picture of what looked like a cossack and his wife. 

Her eyes would suddenly stop, admiring it. The refined deportment of the cavalryman, the dress of the woman. 

"Fuck are you waiting for? Can we sell anything, or fucking not?" Arseniy kept his rifle aimed at the woods, turning in circles, waiting for any possible looters to come and take their 'prey'. 

"Yeah... probably." Catherine would take the photo out, crumple it, and stick it into the bullet hole in the officer's head, cackling as she stuffed the cigarette case into her pocket. 

"Let's go. Nothing left of these losers, and soon the wolves will start swarming for them." The two would begin walking away, as the two bodies began to freeze in the snow.

options.name: In a world of insanity, nothing is sacred.

title: The Two Hounds
desc:
Usoyan wrinkled his nose at the smell of cigar smoke and alcohol as he opened the door into the darkened depths of the Great Pakhan's office. 

Ioseliani was asleep again, his dirty boots propped up on the desk as he lay back in his leather armchair, the cap pushed down over his eyes. The Kurd's jaw clenched as he walked up to the desk, and cleared his throat. 

"Pakahn Ioseliani." 

Ioseliani would grumble something similar to a swear under his breath and slowly push the visor above his eyes with his index finger. 

"Hm? Ah... Usoyen?" 

"Usoyan." 

The Great Pakhan smirked, finding his purposeful mispronunciation somehow humorous, Usoyan's lips thinned out as he placed the paper list in front of Ioseliani. 

"Here's a list of the newly ascended pakhans in the last month, to share." 

Ioseliani yawned, grabbing the list lazily, his eyes beginning to scan the names, and absent-mindedly pronouncing, "Bit of whiskey?" 

"I do not drink on workdays." The Kurd responded curtly. 

"Then take a seat-" 

"I have no time to LAZE around AIMLESSLY." 

Now this DID cause Ioseliani to raise his eyes from the list, measuring Usoyan up predatorily, before snorting and tossing the list onto the desk in front of him. 

"Well, if you did your job better, Usoyen, maybe you WOULD have the time. You're missing Popov and Kikvadze, next time double-check your shit before waking me up." 

The Great Pakhan would lean back into the leather chair yet again, and nonchalantly push the cap back over his eyes, signalling the conversation was over and that Usoyan should take his leave. 

Barely containing his frustration, with teeth grinding, Usoyan left the office. In that moment, both of them shared only one thing in common. One thought. One phrase.

title: A Loyal Servant
desc:
"Check-mate." Usoyan placed the weathered piece forward, Ilo's eyes bulging as he silently mouthed to himself, taking in the whole board, before finally seeing how his King was locked into place and put down, sighing and scratching the back of his head. 

"Good game, sir." The right-hand man would stand up and straighten the creases on his grey jacket and corrected his worn tie. 

"Certainly." The Kurd swiped the pieces into the chess box and shut it, putting it away emotionlessly. 

Usoyan did not like the ruffle and dirt of the average bandits, those more reminding him of some mentally deficient green army peasants he heard so many stories of in his childhood. But Ilo Devdari signified the complete opposite, the man almost always well-groomed, eloquent and most importantly, still retaining his deadliness. 

"Anyways, while it was a good break from my duty, sir, I need to get onto the task you gave me." Ilo would take out a cigarette, but noticing Usoyan's grimace would silently place it back in his pocket, not requiring a worded complaint. 

And yet, for all of the man's similarities to a Cosa Nostra grunt, or a corporate dog that Usoyan wanted to emulate in his men, there was still that unbreakable lingering smell of shit, un-business-like activities, self-indulgence... 

"Of course, Rafael Baghdasaryan... Keep track of him, if you may. The man may seem weak-willed, but considering that he works under that oaf, he probably has several surprises that I would prefer to be neutered when the time comes." 

Ilo took out his butterfly knife, the 'feather' whistling as he flipped it open, "And if he is open for a 'present', so to say?" 

The Kurd smiled.

title: Deep Cuts
desc:
"What did you say about my mother, you fucking katzap!?" Ayaz hissed, standing up from his kneeling position next to the bottle of cheap-shit beer he and his mates had decided to share. 

"I called her a whore, a fucking whore, kozyol!" Vanya 'Scissors' gave his brand smile, his hand travelling to his pocket, his weapon of choice in the form of sheep sheers resting comfortably in his hand. 

"Van'ka, I don't think it's worth it..." Dmitry on the other hand did not keep anything in his pockets, but as a right-hand man of the small gang of delinquents, he had to be present for what essentially came down to a dick-measuring contest. 

"Shut it! It's just getting interesting!" Scissors hissed through his teeth, turning back to Ayaz. "So, you fucking sheep-fucker, what are you gonna do about it!? Or what," Vanya nodded to the side, turning the opposing gang's attention to the rest of the dozen-or-so other young men, several armed with rusty pipes or broken bottles. ", Don't got the guts?" 

"You really," Ayaz, infamous for his rage, bit his tongue, barely containing himself, "REALLY don't want this!" The roar alarmed the rest of his gang, several also standing up, picking up bricks and bottles. 

"Van'ka... stop..." Dmitry reflexively took a stance, his hand finding the gas pistol in the inside of his pocket. 

"You keep shitting yourself, you'll be sitting in it for the rest of your life!" Scissors grinned, "Let's fucking go!" And burst forward. 

The fight was short, and ugly, several Russians falling to the ground from the gas rounds and holding onto their knocked around heads, same as several Turks, the gangs dispersing when no one had the strength to continue. 

"See? SEE THAT! MIT'KA!" Vanya wheezed from exhaustion, looking around for his 'right-hand'. "That's the shit! That's the-!" His tirade was disturbed with a pained groan. 

"Mit'ka..?"

options.name: "Oh fuck, Van'ka, COFF, I can't- I can't stop stop bleeding..."

title: Low Marks Again
desc:
"Sorry, Marya Stepanovna, real sorry!" The young man dragged Dmitry through the doorway of the single room apartment, past the stone-faced Marya, the middle-aged woman not even having time to take off her apron. 

"They jumped us, I wasn't even sure if-" 

"Don't worry, Vasya, just go on, your mother is also worried sick." The woman pronounced evenly, helping Dmitry sit down, the 17-year-old grunting uncharacteristically for his age as if he was an old man and everything hurt. 

Vasya would nod nervously, looking back at Dmitry, "H-heh, I guess I'll see you tomorrow, M-mit'ka! Gotta go, haha!" He would slip out of the apartment as quickly as possible, leaving his comrade alone. 

Marya would unclip the young man's shirt, finding the sewing kit in the back of the kitchen and then finding the knife injury on his stomach.  

"Lord, blood and a hole, you have really made a mess of the shirt, Myten'ka..." Her stone-cold tone would warm slightly but her voice began to shake. 

Dmitry grunted something acknowledging, his cap having slid down to his eyes as he put his weight against the table, it being hard to even sit down.  

Beginning to sew the wound shut, Marya Stepanovna would look at the rest of the scars that littered her son's chest and arms, the same ones she also had to close. "Lord, Mitya, this CANNOT continue..." 

"Mhm..." The other responded weakly. 

"Do you not even think!? Do you think that burying on man in the family is not enough!? Want to make me have to bury my son as well!?" 

"No, Ma..." 

"Lord, I do not even know what to do with you anymore! You wander about with those boys, you make a mess! Why can you not be like your sister!? Do you want to bring me to an early grave, Mit'ya!?" 

"No, Ma, no..." 

"All you know is fight and fight and fight, and we have to all clean it up and bear it! When will you grow up!?" Marya would throw the sewing kit down, having sewn his wound shut, and sit down, putting her face in her hands. 

Dmitry opened his mouth, only one weak excuse flowing out.

title: Fear the Quiet Ones
desc:
"So what is this about?" Nursultan grimaced at Rafael, the man sitting relaxedly in the forest clearing, picking at something in his shoe sole with a small stick. "I got a feast to get back to." 

"O-of course, Mister Tynyshbaev, of course. Though I would suggest your men lower their rifles." Rafael did not lift his gaze, continuing to look at his shoe, ignoring the two men that flanked the Kazakh pakhan. 

"Eh heh heh, no way. There's a little resistance going on with you higher-ups. I ain't got anything to hide, but I ain't letting you go through my corpse's pocket either." Nursultan sneered, not moving from his place, "Say your piece, and I'm off." 

Rafael sighed, scratching his head nervously, "Well, this is quite uncomfortable, but I do have to ask..." 

"Go on..." The pakhan suddenly garnered the feeling that he was being watched but overlooked it. Rafael was famous for his cowardice and straightforwardness, it surprised the Kazakh how he had stayed Ioseliani's right hand for so long. 

"W-well, how do I say this, as I remember that you had to loot several cities with an established capacity of around... 50 thousand rounds, was it? Forgive me, my ammunition c-counting abilities have gone down recently." 

Nursultan clenched his jaw, giving a signal with a cross of his arms for the bodyguards to prepare to shoot, "Yeah, I paid out the promised 10 to the Great Pakhan's forces, why?" 

"Y-yes, well, several of your men had reported to me about a certain deal with extra-bandital-" The Kazakh's blood had gone cold.  

"Fire! FUCKING FI-" Nursultan's order was cut short with a knife to the side and the sound of gunfire behind him, one of his bodyguard's dropping dead, the pakhan sinking to his knee and hissing from the pain of the 'feather' stuck between his ribs. 

"Good work, Ryakhtyashev." He could not recognize the unsure voice of Rafael Bagdasarian, which instead suddenly grew even and cold. "Now." 

A small choir of rifle clicks sounded from behind the tree line, several dozen bandits stepping forward, circling around Nursultan.

options.name: "Why don't we talk on the terms I prefer, Mister Tynyshbaev?"

title: Judgement
desc:
Kazimir pleaded desperately, but it was no use as the bastards sneered at him, laughed at him as the 'crimes' he had supposedly committed were read out, one by one. How had he ever gotten into this situation? When did the bastards get so organized?" 

"Kazimir Kozlov, for ten counts of homosexuality, three counts of treason, and one count each of murder, rape and incest, you are sentenced to death!" The rascal in the centre dressed like a judge boomed, slamming a makeshift gavel onto the table in front of him. He could only gape as the whoops and cheers got louder and louder until he was grabbed by the scruff of his neck by several scrawny henchmen, and dragged off the 'court' just as an assortment of fruit began to be pelted at him. 

Blindfolded and handcuffed, the panicking man could only sputter out desperate insults, looking for a chance, any chance for them to let go of him so he could make a break for it. 

"Not so cocky now, aren't cha?" A familiar voice to his right muttered menacingly, "I'll never forget the day you murdered my friends, you fucking coward!" 

Kazimir groaned as he was shoved to the ground roughly, feeling something sharp graze his thighs as he tumbled to the floor. "Say hello," a second voice said, "To your new home until you die, coward!" His blindfold was swiftly removed, and realization set in quickly as Kazimir stared at the pit of cement ahead of him. 

The former guard who could kill emotionlessly could barely speak coherent sentences as he  was reduced to quite the sorry state, begging for his life and breaking down in tears as he used every last ounce of energy he had attempting to break free of the thieves' iron grip but to no avail. "Please, let m-me go! I'll do a-anything, I swear! I'll be your slave! I-I'll clean your toilets! I'll d-do anything, so please d-don't kill me-!" 

His pleas for help were promptly silenced as he was dumped in the pit, his final minutes spent flailing pathetically in the rapidly hardening cement, much to the amusement of the bandits. The poor man would continue to sink deeper and deeper into the pit, until all that was left uncovered would be a single hand sticking out of the now solid pool of cement, frozen and unmoving.

title: The Kurdish Spider
desc:
'Uncle' Aslan Usoyan looked at himself in the mirror, straightening the creases on his newly smuggled leather jacket. 

"Sir..?" The bandit mercenary stood impatiently in front of the bespoke wooden desk, the cigarette he burst in with still seeping a thin line of smoke, his dirtied appearance and bloodied nose looking out of place in the neat office-like room. 

"..." Aslan would turn around, sitting down at his desk, grimacing at the cigarette. "What is it?" 

"There has been a request from the Great Pakhan, sir." The bandit cleared his throat, "It's an ammunition problem." 

"Go on." Usoyan already knew where this was going, but preferred to not jump to the unpleasant conclusion. 

"We're in a skirmish around the Sverdlovsk region, it got big, too big. The Great Pakhan requests ammunition and considers your business and status capable enough to provide both the ammunition and transportation." 

Usoyan, already annoyed, felt his mood plummet. "And when would the Great Pakhan like that delivery?" 

"Now." The bandit took out the cigarette, knocking some ashes off of it onto the floor, placing it back between his lips. 

A tense silence. Usoyan clenched his jaw. "He will have the ammunition in around 3 hours, I have a local branch there, they should have the surplus transported quickly." 

"Thank you, sir." The bandit turned around, trudging out of the office, his boots leaving visible dirt marks on the floor. 

Usoyan waited for him to leave, before sighing and sitting forward, interlocking his fingers, "Fucking animals..."

options.name: Even the strongest web cannot withstand a determined brute.

title: Just another Day
desc:
In the wee hours of the morning, multiple border guards would suddenly be dragged out of sleep by the sounds of gunfire, battle cries, and the rumbling of vehicles as the bandits stabbed deep into the Aviators' territory for the second time that week. The adults would scramble to dust off their rifles while their children would be taken far away from their homes to escape the incoming bloodbath. 

Then, the fighting. The bastards would storm the town, setting homes alight as they grabbed anything that appeared even the slightest bit valuable. Valiant men and women would waste their lives defending what little possessions they had left, sacrificing themselves as the raiders would move further inland, taking more and more. But just as hope appeared lost, they would suddenly retreat to their dens with their arms full of stolen loot, disappearing within mere minutes. And in an hour, the only proof that they were ever there would be the cooling bodies on the floor and the destruction they had wrought in their short stay. 

The children would return to their town to find Papa and Mama bleeding out in the cold Russian snow and their homes reduced to little more than burning cinders in the dirt. But as life must go on, the survivors would rebuild, attempting to remake their homes and plant more crops, only to be attacked again next week. 

Such is life in the Russian Anarchy.

options.name: Their resources are put to better use in our hands.

title: Heroes of Old
desc:
Yevdokia tested the dent between her teeth, cringing at the feeling of the newly missing tooth having been knocked out when her face met the plane's dashboard. The last few hours she maintained a stoic front, but the frustration simmered under her. 

In what world would they have won against these maniacs? If they didn't keep the much-needed anti-air at their airbases to protect the planes that got turned against them when the criminals took their airports? If they had guarded the couple dozen of planes the rats got away with better, would they have not failed..? 

Well, it didn't matter in the end. Her fingers found the charred photo of Konstantin she had always kept in her pocket. Bayonets, bullets, execution... at least she would see him again... 

The metal door of the cell slammed, her softened expression hardening again. At least she would meet her end bravely. 

The King Rat, in all his debauched glory, drunk, entered the room, sitting down across the pilot. 

Sighing, Ioseliani observed Yevdokia's face, chuckling. "Fuck me, sorry about the face, but the boys DID have to take down your plane." Putting his hand in his pocket, he would take out a metal flask placing it in front of her. 

"Vodka, we ain't got painkillers on hand, so that's the best I can do for now-" 

"Just get it over with."  

Ioseliani blinked, "Say that again..?" 

Yevdokia turned her smashed face away from the flask disgustedly. "I know men like you, no honor, so just end it with the semantics and take me out..." 

Ioseliani paused, before taking the flask and taking a rapid swig himself, before chuckling. 

"What, you think just 'cause we stole your planes we want you dead? It's a dog eat dog world out there! Heh, you shot down the bomber bastards, so relax,"

options.name: "The term of 'hero' ain't foreign to us."

title: Airforce Tango
desc:
Ulyana felt the bead of sweat run down her temple as the MiG-3 Interceptor engine roared in front of her, the night whistling past behind the cockpit glass. An attack... an attack... 

Sure, there were raids on them, everyone was getting raided in this Hell that used to be called the Soviet Union. But no one ever tried to occupy them, no one had the manpower, the motivation, the strength, and yet the panicked look on her officer's face when he said to lift off said everything... 

Her eyes caught out a small light in the distance. It was one of theirs, but why was it flying in the opposite direction..? 

The radio whined, "Oh SHIT it's them! THOSE'RE THE PLANES THAT GOT STOLE-" 

RATATA- 

Ulyana nosedived as several rounds ricocheted off of the wings off of her interceptor, some fifth sense that she developed over the hundreds of flights telling her she was being followed. 

The radio distorted, a male voice coming through, "Gahaha! So that's the frequency you got! Let's dance, ladies!" 

Ulyana grimaced, pulling up, doing a Nesterov loop maneuvre, the darkness of the night causing the Thief interceptor to miss her, the dogfight flipping as she was able to take the following position, hammering his tail. 

"Gah, ya lil bitch!" The radio whined, it seemed the thieves were intent on insulting them even if they were about to go down, "Well, how about this-!" 

The Thief before her pulled up as she followed, suddenly his engine going silent, Ulyana passing him as the thief plane fell back to Earth, disappearing into the cloud cover. 

Had she won? It was at least a dozen seconds of attentive observation when- 

RATATAT- 

A round slammed near her cockpit, the sound of the engine appearing behind her, the radio crackling. "Cunts like you never see THIS one coming, GAHA GAHA!" Whatever manoeuvre he did, Ulyana did not see something so unorthodox before... This wasn't going to be easy.

title: Beware the Mannered Ones
desc:
Ilo corrected his tie, the well-groomed right-hand man looking out of place in the Circle's meeting place, surrounded by a few of the pakhan's who were receptive to his offers and calls, some arriving with their own men. 

"So what's this shit about? You said you were going to offer us something, WELL, GO AHEAD!" Pavel 'Flint' Kamenev tossed the cigarette aside and coughed into his hand.  

Ilo looked around, before smiling, "Gentlemen, as we all know you are all indebted to my employer, be it ammunition, men or other amenities you have ordered, so Mister Usoyan has been wonderful enough as to FORGIVE YOUR DEBTS!" Ilo threw his hands to his sides, several satisfied murmurs coming out of the crowd. 

"So that's it..? Couldn't that Kurdish fuck just sent a runner or radio'd." Pavel sighed standing up, his men on the other hand not moving an inch. 

"I did not finish, please sit down." Ilo pronounced, his expression flicking to a sudden cold stoniness, Pavel's bodyguards taking their rifles and aiming at their own pakhan. 

"Wh-" Kamenev lifted his hands, a mix of shock and rage tearing through his exterior. 

"Sit. Down." Ilo's face was now blank as he eyed Kamenev emotionlessly, "Sit. Down. Or your own men will blow your head open and one of them will replace you for it..." 

Pavel's hands tightened into fists as he sat down, his 'bodyguards' standing by his side, the other pakhan's also silent, the air of mistrust rippling through the Circle. 

"As I was saying, we are forgiving all your debts, but that must come with a price, that being a small decrease in autonomy." Ilo pronounced cheerfully, "As you can see on Mister Pavel's case, we already have you by your throat, so could you be so kind as to-" 

Ilo's grin extended up to his ears, yet his eyes weren't smiling.

title: In With The... Older
desc:
Anatoly Cherkasov dropped the rifle into the corner of the room like a student drops a school bag after a long day, nodding to the Great Pakhan and then acknowledging Batov with a confused look. 

"Afternoon sir, what have you called me in for?" 

Ioseliani was laid back in his armchair, his boots up on the desk, though he was slightly less drunk than usual, eyeing Anatoly with a smirk. 

"Well, let's rip the 'splinter' out, Cherkasov, you're demoted." 

The Great Pakhan's words rippled through Cherkasov, the casual pronunciation of the life-changing order filling him with even greater hopelessness. 

"Sir, I-" 

"From now on, you are not Security Minister, you are a general. Now fuck off, that's all I had to say."  

"Sir, I served... we took Vorkuta, we took Zlatoust, I do not understand-" 

Ioseliani's expression changed as he sat forward and stood up, rolling open a map, lines all over it. "See that's why you're going out, Tolya, you don't understand SHIT." 

Ioseliani's hand went over the map, before slamming a fist down on the piece of paper, "THIS! This was your operation to take Zlatoust, and guess what, Tolya, if I had THAT man," Ioseliani's finger lifted pointing at Batov, "In your seat, we'd have taken it FASTER, SAFER and CHEAPER. That's not a 'maybe' Tolya, you're just shittier, so if you were about to argue, shut your FUCKING trap and be happy that your skills are enough to keep you as general, GOT IT?" 

Cherkasov turned from red to blue, to a snow-white pale. "C-certainly... sir..." Anatoly lifted his eyes, nodding to Batov, "Good luck..." The ex-Security Minister stumbled out of the room, forgetting his rifle. 

A short silence. Batov opened his mouth. "That was one way to dismiss a minister..."  

Ioseliani grimaced, sitting back down into the armchair, "For all my love, when it comes to the army,"

title: I Shall Return...
desc:
Batov leaned down in the car as several bullets ricocheted off of the truck's door, the driver's look turning to panic, the only thing stopping him from turning to look was the discipline hammered into him. 

"Sir, are you-!" 

"Keep driving, damn it!" 

Getting back up, Batov leaned out of the truck window and fired a couple of rounds at those following them, one of the trucks swerving off of the road as the bandit driver on their tail visibly sagged in his seat. 

"We're almost at the border!" 

Batov's concentrated expression persisted as he fired a couple more rounds. "Do you see their border guard?" 

"I do!" 

"Good, if we play our cards right, they'll focus on the Usoyani before they try to follow us!"  

300 meters. Several of the army men at the checkpoint would notice their approach. 200 meters. Batov did not look back at where they were driving, using the extra seconds to chamber another round, still leaning out of the window. 100... Batov ran out of ammo in the magazine, getting back inside. 

0 

The truck's front smashed through the barrier before the blockade trucks were able to shut off the escape route, machine gun's roaring as they started up just a little too late, the General's pursuers caught in the fire. 

The truck continued a couple of minutes before turning off the road into the forest, the driver and Batov checking for damage. 

"So... what now?" 

Batov raised his eyes. "Now? Now we try to find out way..."

options.name: "Maybe even a way back, when the time comes..."

title: A Damned Mess
desc:
Usoyan felt a headache travel up his temples. 

"Say that again..." 

"He escaped, sir..." Ilo somehow looked even more disappointed than his employer, and even more, shaken up, his tie crumpled, "Everything was ready. The officers were bought off, the ammunition was taken away... If it wasn't for one of those cowards defecting to him, we would have succeeded..." 

"..." Usoyan did not respond his gaze cast thoughtfully into the distance. 

Ilo took it as rage, "I... I am ready to take full responsibility..." 

The Kurd snapped out of it, standing up, "Enough. For all the mess you have created, the main goal has been achieved. For all intended purposes, the army is ours. And besides-" Usoyan walked around the table, slapping Ilo on the shoulder in an uncommonly friendly manner. 

"That soldafon was always a slimy piece of work. Just getting him out is an achievement."  

Ilo blinked surprisedly, "Th-thank you, sir."  

"Alright," The Kurd straightened the creases on his jacket, clearing his throat, "Without the army, that he is alone." 

For once, Usoyan smiled.

title: Gone Full Circle
desc:
Anatoly Cherkasov couldn't tell what he felt when he entered the office that used to belong to the Great Pakhan, now taken over by Usoyan. The whole space has become much cleaner, not a single empty bottle, loose document or even speck of dust on the surfaces of the tables and bookcases. 

"You have called me, sir?" 

While his demotion from Security Minister under Ioseliani had been humiliating, he was not sure what to expect now. When the coup occurred, several generals had thought of defecting, of escaping, of following Batov... but even with all the respect Cherkasov had for the man, the dent on his pride began to burn with an even greater strength than before. 

He stayed. And now, He would have to see what they would do to him. Though, he considered, dying for spite is also a foolish thing, really... 

Usoyan rose from his seat. "I have good news for you, Mister Cherkasov. While several of your colleagues had abandoned post, and attempted to resist the coming of a better Russia, you had stayed loyal to Yugra." The businessman walked up to the thief general, offering his hand for a shake. 

"We appreciate the loyalty, Mister Cherkasov."  

Anatoly blinked, shaking the hand absentmindedly, still feeling a little starstruck that the new ruler had noticed him so well... 

"And for loyalty there is reward. We offer you the spot of Security Minister, which has been taken away from you so unceremoniously." 

Cherkasov suddenly sensed the fake on Usoyan's face. While the lips were smiling, the eyes were empty. In the end... 

"Thank you, sir, I will begin my duties then..." 

Usoyan nodded, "Very well, I would like a report by tomorrow morning." Cherkasov turned on his heel, marching out of the room, jaw clenched, wandering... no, knowing that if Batov was here then...

title: We’re Cutting You Off
desc:
“What do you MEAN he refused!” Ioseliani sat up, his expression changing from the usual self-assuredness to a terrifying grimace. 

Rafael unconsciously took a step back at that look, forcing the words out of himself, “H-he said that there was not enough ammunition in the depots, and even if he got a new batch, it would take too long to transport.” 

The Great Pakhan smashed his fist down on his table. “BULLSHIT! He lied!” 

Rafael could not disagree completely, but he could not let Ioseliani to storm out and do something overly violent. “Our borders did expand, s-sir...” 

“Fuck your borders, Raf! We never had problems with garnering emergency equipment and ammunition when our boys were on the back foot in a raid, and NOW, SUDDENLY, that damned Kurd is giving us a radio silence and then no apology!? Am I supposed to FUCKING swallow that?!” Ioseliani sat down again, fuming, putting his thumbnail between his teeth as he considered something. 

... 

“Sir?” Rafael calmed a little at the silence but seeing Ioseliani’s state was disturbing. 

“I want that bastard to drown in paperwork...” 

“Pardon?” 

The Great Pakhan lifted his eyes, his voice threateningly low, “Drown that bastard. Paperwork, security checks, the boredom and vandalism of the patrolling soldiers, I don’t care, make his company choke on the Thief Territories, give prime passage to our supply trucks.”

title: All Paths Grow Thorns
desc:
Usoyan paced his office as Ilo read off the list. 

“Two food trucks, several tonnes of small arms ammunition, a seized ammunition depot-” 

“Enough.” The Kurd stopped in his tracks, turning on his heel, staring down his right-hand man, “Well?” 

Ilo corrected his tie nervously, blinking a couple of times, “Well... what, sir?” 

“What did that oaf respond to our demands?” Usoyan rounded his desk, sitting down and interlocking his fingers. “When will this stop?” 

“Uh... well...” Ilo opened the crumpled note clipped to the notebook, clearing his throat, “I quote, ‘Let the boys have some fun, a few missing bullets is no harm done’-” 

“Madness... UTTER MADNESS!” The Kurd interrupted his assistant standing again, measuring the room with his steps, “That is not a lack of discipline! Who does that brute take me for!?” 

Ilo waited for a pause in the tirade, “You are certainly correct. The destruction of assets in such a massive wave is unlikely to be-” 

“I know Ilo, I know, no need to REPEAT MY THOUGHTS.” Usoyan rubbed his temples. 

“This must end, put all drivers on the smuggling routes, off the main roads. No more ‘emergency aid’, I want you to crush his suck-ups’ skulls. Starve them of EVERYTHING! The export will make up for it!”

options.name: “That animal will be paying his debts, three-fold!”

title: Opposites Do Not Attract
desc:
Ilo stepped through the door of the office, dodging the blade that flew past his face. 

“Who the fu-” Ioseliani slurred as he got up from his seat, his hand reaching for the gun, Ilo, on the other hand smiling back at the Great Pakhan. 

“Ooooh, it’s the tuxedo thundercunt,” Ioseliani plopped back into his seat, clearly not a morning man, considering the slight hangover he had. 

“Good morning, Mister Ioseliani, I see you have not lost your reflexes.” Ilo swiped some dust off of his jacket and corrected his tie machinally. 

“No, no I haven’t, and if you don’t want ‘em to be used on you, you better start talking.” Ioseliani sneered as he pronounced the threat, taking a sip of his bottle. 

“We both know the...” 

“Fucked situation.” The Great Pakhan cut in. 

“I would say... strained... but that is besides the point.” Ilo walked up to the desk, placing a paper down. “I have come to probe if you were open to a diplomatic resolution, hm?” 

Ioseliani grimaced at Ilo, sitting back in his armchair. “I know what Usoyan sees himself as, thundercunt. He’d own everything if he could. And I don’t see my life extending far beyond him taking power, ANY power. So whatever you have written... Nah, no. Go tell your sugar daddy that I’m not interested.” 

Ilo clenched his jaw, leaving the paper lying down, “So you would not even consider looking at it?” 

“No.” 

Ilo blinked, “Well, I suppose I shall take my leave then...” The right-hand man turned on his heel- 

“Yeah, and take your blank piece of paper with you.” Ioseliani tossed the ‘diplomatic resolution’ across the room, “Next time, have the balls to at least fake a call to diplomacy to probe me.” 

Ilo did not respond, instead disappearing behind the doors.

title: Strive for Better
desc:
“And so, in a pincer motion one can...” Batov moved his finger on the map, the newly-minted generals staring at him with undivided attention, from Pechurin’s sleazy kleptomaniac eyes, to Avramov’s melancholic gaze. None of these officers even had a formal education, some of them barely knew how to read, however Batov did see a lot of potential in some, enough to take in as proteges after the general troop reform had begun. 

Kyril ‘Korobka’ may have been a smuggler, however if there was anyone who understood the struggle of the supply question, it was him. When running through theory, the man had the utmost understanding of where to utilize firepower, and where to preserve the infrastructure, glistening with his golden teeth as he grinned slightly greedily. 

Avramov, for his reputation as a constant escapee, had a good consideration for terrain, especially on the defense and the retreat, his home turf being the forests. “Well, we get the boys to the treeline, and Avos’ will carry us through, sire...” He tended to pronounce any time a tactical situation discussion was brought up, seemingly not completely realising that not everyone was as well acclimated to the natural barriers of the Motherland. 

Pechurin, on the other hand, had a great understanding for attack, the man’s grabby hand tightening into fists excitedly every time tanks or artillery were brought up. Considering the man’s reputation as a robber and a small arms enthusiast, it did make sense. 

“There we are, for today, the lecture is over, return to your barracks.” Batov rolled the map closed, watching the ex-bandits salute and begin to march out. 

He noticed something and sighed... maybe calling them ‘EX’-bandits was still a bit too early. 

“Pechurin.” The thief stopped at his name being called, turning on his heel, clearly guilty. 

“Return my wrist-watch, and please keep this mania of yours under control next time.” Batov lectured exhaustedly. The watch clacked as it was placed on the desk and the thief slipped out of the room nervously.

options.name: “Can beat a general into a thief, but not a thief out of a general.”

title: Death to Oligopoly
desc:
Har’kov couldn’t stop the trembling. 

“Ch-christ j-just b-b-be a m-m-man...” Even whispering insults to himself to man up didn’t work. His mental state seemed to be faring the worst in the group that was sat against the wall. 

Some of them he could not recognize, but others were sheer magnates. Fayzulin, considered one of the main bankers in all of Zlatoust, didn’t seem to mind the uncomfortable position against the brick wall, instead looking up thoughtfully at the grey sky. Kozlov, the owner of several local steel manufacturers also seemed to be calm, writing something in his journal, his hand moving gracefully across the page. 

And then Har’kov. What did they want from HIM? He was a confectioner, a small one at that. He’s a nobody. Just sold sweets around Zlatoust, exported a bit to Komi before that one turned into the mess it was. WHAT. DID. THEY. WANT??? 

Trying not to panic, he bit into his nails as several bandit guards entered the small courtyard, machine guns over their shoulders. 

One of them, with a facial scar, looked over the list in his hand, looking up at the businessmen. 

“Anyone with less than half a million rubles profit?”  

Wait... Half a million? Har’kov never made beyond A QUARTER. 

“M-me! M-ME!” He shouted anxiously waving his hand, followed by several others in the line. 

“Well, come forward!” The scarface grinned, waving them behind the line of machine guns, Har’kov not sparing a second as he power-walked past the guards, up to scarface. 

“So, what do you do?” Scarface took out a pen, looking at the confectioner and the several other nobodies in a line behind him. 

“I-I’m a confectioner.” 

“Oh, confectioner?” There was a clack behind Har’kov’s back and he felt himself jump as the thundering roar of machine guns blasted into his ears. 

“Heh, we’ll need those, I guess.” The scarface signed the slip, pushing it into Har’kov’s hand. “Free to go, now fuck off.” 

As the confectioner walked out, his heart nearly bursting, he gave one last look behind him, at the ones left in line. Fayzulin’s body sagged against the wall, his expression calm and unreadable.

title: Clerical Errors
desc:
“Raf, what exactly do these papers mean?” The Great Pakhan shuffled for his reading glasses, looking visibly confused at what exactly the sheet of graphs and numbers laying on his desk meant. 

“Jaba, in just the last week, 2 million rubles have disappeared from accounts associated with you and our loyalists across the Territory. Though we haven’t been able to trace who’s received the money, we can only assume that it’s the reason behind our informants within Usoyan’s circle warning us of increased arms purchases as of late.” 

“I need every hand we can get on finding out who’s getting the damn money, Raf. Now! They’re planning something big, I just know it, and if we don’t flush out that Kurdish bastard’s rats now he’ll not just have my head, but yours! Do you even give a damn Rafael?”  Sweat rolled down the Great Pakhan’s face as Jaba’s temper gave out.  

“Of course, Jaba, I care! You think Aslan won’t have me in a gutter if he takes you out? But please, listen.  When you get like this we can’t get anything done.” Nodding his head in understanding, Jaba at last calmed down a bit to get back to the papers. One thing in particular caught his eye in particular. Some ex-collective farms in the Tyumen oblast that were given to supposed “compliant figures” had received a strangely high influx of funding for “private agricultural development”. It couldn’t have been a coincidence then, that the owners of these farms had alleged ties to a certain Aslan Usoyan. 

“Raf, look here.  A couple of well placed bribes here and there could uncover the whole nest of snakes.  This guy here, Pavel Mikhailovich, ehh..m.” The Pakhan took a pause to emphasize, “might need some...convincing. I trust that you will get the right people on the job, and that these friends of that Kurdish son of a bitch will soon be dog food, as God willing soon he will be too. Jaba looked Rafael straight in the eyes as he left the room, and had only one thing left to say:

title: A Deeper Consideration
desc:
“And so, and so I tell him, GAHAHAHA-!” Ioseliani smashed his glass down on the table bursting into a drunken roar-like laughter. Batov gave a polite chuckle but kept the glass of whisky away from his lips, instead crossing his arms and sloshing the liquid with slow motions of his wrist. 

The warm light of the old lightbulbs poured across the room of the general’s quarters. For once, the Great Pakhan had decided to visit, instead of calling the General to his office, the two men’s drinking parties mostly devolving into Batov politely listening to Ioseliani’s roaring epics, fictional or not. 

“Gehe, gehe, so that’s why I don’t trust no equipment past its due date, heh.” Ioseliani wiped his eyes from the laughter tears and sipped a bit more from his glass. 

“Curious.” Batov pronounced absent-mindedly, his gaze focused on the window. 

Ioseliani lifted his gaze, his mood swinging drunkenly. “What? Don’t like my story?” 

“No, no. A rather curious thing, I was just thinking back to something...” 

“Well spill! Damned soldafon, I ain’t the KGB!”  

Batov shrugged off the insult. “I recently decided to create a Scout Corps, I have experience myself, they can be useful. Of course, I needed young men for the job, putting veterans as scouts can be harmful.” 

“Get oooooooon with it.” 

“Something struck me about those recruits. When I was recruited as a scout for the Leib Guard, back in 1915, they had been in the same exact sorry state. Boys, who could nary read or write, had broken teeth and signs of malnutrition. And sometimes... I do wonder...” Batov paused. 

“Weeeeeeeeeell?” 

Ioseliani’s questioning got on the General’s nerves, “I do wonder if for all I know, I’m just installing another Tzar into place.” 

Another silence. Ioseliani’s expression turned grim as he sat back in the wooden chair and rubbed his face thoughtfully.  

“Weeeell, I ain’t the best man out there... but I ain’t no Tzar.” He smirked. “Just ‘cause we’re gonna make pakhans rule the country don’t mean we’re not gonna be accountable to someone... Yeah, yeah! Ain’t gonna be a pakhan who doesn’t serve the people!” 

Batov chuckled at the newly-found drunken enthusiasm, before looking off thoughtfully.
